STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.claim: Its themes include God's power over nature and repeated warnings of punishment on earth or in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.anchor: references to God’s Power over the natural world (vv. 66–70), repeated warnings to human beings about the coming of Divine Punishment

STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r8.claim: Verses 70–76 portray the Prophet nearly yielding to idolaters' effort to divert him from revelation, but God makes him firm.
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r8.anchor: the Prophet is said to have nearly succumbed to the idolaters’ attempt to lead him away from the revelations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Human honour and provision should prompt gratitude rather than Satan-like arrogance; human superiority over other species is limited, since other creatures may be superior.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the honour mentioned in this verse entails that they must remember these favours of God and instead of showing arrogance, be grateful to Him.

BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r1.claim: The words honor and honoring share the meaning of dignity and generosity; Abu al-Su'ud says this dignity covers all children of Adam, righteous and wicked.
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r1.anchor: قال المولى أبو السعود : بني آدم قاطبة تكريما شاملا لبرهم وفاجرهم

BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r2.claim: The inward commentary divides honor into bodily and spiritual kinds. Bodily honor, shared by all, includes God's fashioning Adam's clay and forming people beautifully, upright and equipped for skilled action.
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : خصصناهم بكرامة تخرجهم من حيز الاشتراك وهي على ضربين

BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r3.claim: Common spiritual honor includes God's breath, teaching the names, the primordial covenant, fitra, messengers, books, signs, and promises of Paradise with warnings of the Fire; special honor is prophethood, sainthood, faith, guidance, and spiritual ascent.
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r3.anchor: وهي أن كرمه بنفخه فيه من روحه وعلمه الأسماء كلها وكلمه قبل أن خلقه

BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r4.speaker: قشيري
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r4.claim: Qushayri takes “children of Adam” here to mean believers, since God humiliates the unbeliever so no one can honor him.
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r4.anchor: امام قشيري قدس سره فرموده كه مراد از بني آدم مؤنا نند ه كافرانرا

BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r5.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r5.claim: The outward honor is faith and righteous action; a believer is more honored by God than a near angel. Muhammad ibn Ka'b says humanity is honored because Muhammad is one of them.
BURSEVI:v5p141#2/r5.anchor: كما قال في "بحر العلوم" الظاهر عندنا تكريمهم بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

BURSEVI:v5p142/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p142/r1.claim: Carrying people on land and sea means providing mounts and ships, a mode of transport unique among creatures.
BURSEVI:v5p142/r1.anchor: من حملته إذا جعلت له ما يركبه وليس من المخلوقات شيء كذلك.

BURSEVI:v5p142/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p142/r2.claim: The inward reading carries people from bodily land and spiritual sea to the shore of lordship; Salami reads the gifts as knowledge and unity, self as land, heart as sea, and manifest versus hidden realities.
BURSEVI:v5p142/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : أي : عبرناهم عن بر الجسمانية وبحر الروحانية

BURSEVI:v5p142/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p142/r3.claim: Good things include varied pleasant provisions produced through human work or otherwise, such as butter, dates, honey, and sweets.
BURSEVI:v5p142/r3.anchor: {من الطيبات} من فنون النعم المستلذة مما يحصل بصنعهم وبغير صنعهم

BURSEVI:v5p142/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p142/r4.claim: For the elect, inward provisions are food of witnessing and drink of unveilings in vessels of gnosis and cups of love, gifts even near angels have not tasted.
BURSEVI:v5p142/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : وهي المواهب التي طيبها من الحدوث

BURSEVI:v5p142/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142/r5.speaker: جامي
BURSEVI:v5p142/r5.claim: Jami's poem says the angels' devotion was surpassed by the outpouring of love upon Adam.

BURSEVI:v5p142/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142/r6.speaker: حافظ
BURSEVI:v5p142/r6.claim: Hafez's poem says angels do not know the story of love and calls for wine and clay to be poured on Adam.

BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r1.claim: Human beings are favored in perception by faculties that distinguish truth from falsehood and good from evil; they should thank God, seek sound belief, and reject shirk.
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r1.anchor: بما ركبنا فيهم من القوى المدركة التي يتميز بها الحق من الباطل

BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r2.claim: Angels are excepted because their knowledge is constant and error-free; the verse concerns a trait shared by all humans, not their relative degree or nearness to God.
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r2.anchor: وإنما استثنى جنس الملائكة من هذا التفضيل لأن علومهم دائمة عارية عن الخطأ

BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r3.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r3.claim: Bahr al-Ulum says Adam and Eve surpass their descendants as original parents, while this does not place humans above near angels.
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r3.anchor: وقال في "بحر العلوم" : فيه دلالة على أن بني آدم فضلوا على كثير

BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r4.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r4.claim: He rejects al-Kalbi, al-Baqillani, and Mu'tazilite claims that angels outrank all humans: the prostration command and Adam's knowledge show otherwise, as does a report of messengers' superiority.
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r4.anchor: كما زعم الكلبي وأبو بكر الباقلاني وحثالة المعتزلة

BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r5.claim: A Prophetic report supports messengers' superiority: an angel failed to rise for Muhammad, so God swore he must stand and remain standing.
BURSEVI:v5p142#2/r5.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "إن الله فضل المرسلين على الملائكة المقربين

BURSEVI:v5p143/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p143/r1.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v5p143/r1.claim: Al-As'ila al-Muqhima says the well-known position of the people of truth is that prophets are superior to angels.
BURSEVI:v5p143/r1.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : المشهور من مذهب أهل الحق أن الأنبياء أفضل

BURSEVI:v5p143/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p143/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p143/r2.claim: Al-Kashifi presents a hierarchy: human progeny outrank angelic messengers, then human saints outrank angelic saints; good believers outrank common angels, who outrank sinful believers.
BURSEVI:v5p143/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (علمارا در تفضيل بشر مباحث دور ودرازاست

BURSEVI:v5p143/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p143/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p143/r3.claim: The inward commentary takes “many” as angels; the perfect human surpasses them by unmediated readiness to receive God's light and bear the trust.
BURSEVI:v5p143/r3.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا} يعني على الملائكة

BURSEVI:v5p143/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p143/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p143/r4.claim: Al-Kashifi describes the complete human as a clear mirror reflecting divine attributes and gathering cosmic particulars into one whole, illustrated by Persian verses.
BURSEVI:v5p143/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وعلى الجملة اين آيت دليل فضيلت وجامعيت انسانست

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.claim: God made all Adam’s descendants, righteous and sinful, noble and endowed with many merits beyond counting.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.anchor: أي جعلناهم قاطبة برهم وفاجرهم ذوي كرم أي شرف ومحاسن جمة لا يحيط بها نطاق الحصر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains human honor as the gift of reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما كرمهم بالعقل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says humans eat with their hands rather than their mouths, unlike other animals.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.anchor: وفي رواية بتناولهم الطعام بأيديهم لا بأفواههم كسائر الحيوانات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the honor is speech.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ attributes the honor to humans’ balanced, upright stature.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies food and pleasures as the special honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r6.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم بالمطاعم واللذات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r7.speaker: يمان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r7.claim: Yamān says the honor is beauty of form.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jarīr says people are honored by being given mastery over other creatures and having them made serviceable.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r8.anchor: وعن ابن جرير بالتسلط على غيرهم من الخلق وتسخيره لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r9.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says the honor includes making Muḥammad one of humankind.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r9.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب بجعل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r10.claim: Other proposals include God creating Adam with His hands, providing for worldly and eternal life, writing, and distinguishing men by beards and women by locks.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : بخلق الله تعالى أباهم آدم بيديه وقيل : بتدبير المعاش والمعاد وقيل : بالخط

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r11.claim: All these honors are illustrative; al-Ālūsī rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s claim that reason alone is intended as contrary to sound reason and transmitted evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r11.anchor: والكل في الحقيقة على سبيل التمثيل ومن ادعى الحصر في واحد كابن عطية حيث قال : إنما التكريم بالعقل لا غير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r12.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī uses the verse to argue that a human being does not become ritually impure upon death.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r12.anchor: ولذا استدل الإمام الشافعي بالآية على عدم نجاسة الآدمي بالموت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r13.claim: Being carried in land and sea means riding on soft-backed animals and dry planks, namely ships; the thing carried upon is understood from context.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p117#2/r13.anchor: على أكباد رطبة وأعواد يابسة من الدواب والسفن فهو من حملته على كذا إذا أعطيته ما يركبه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r1.claim: Another interpretation says God carried humans by keeping them settled in land and sea without sinking or drowning; al-Ālūsī prefers the first as a distinctively human honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r1.anchor: وقيل : المراد من حملهم في البر والبحر جعلهم قارين فيهما بأن لم يخسف بهم الأرض ولم يغرقهم بالماء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r2.claim: The first interpretation better fits the honor because the second is not unique to humans, unlike being carried by animals and ships.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r2.anchor: والأول أنسب بالتكريم إذ لا يثبت لشيء من الحيوانات سواهم بخلاف الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r3.claim: Ṭayyibāt means the varied blessings and desirable things people obtain by their own work or otherwise, including food, clothing, furnishings, and possessions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r3.anchor: أي فنون النعم وضروب المستلذات مما يحصل بصنعهم وبغير صنعهم من المأكولات والملبوسات والمفروشات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r4.claim: Some explain the preference as the honor already mentioned.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that honoring and preference must differ, otherwise the verse repeats itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r5.anchor: وبحث الإمام في هذا المقام بأنه تعالى قال أولا ( ولقد كرمنا بني آدم ) وقال سبحانه هنا ( وفضلناه )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī distinguishes innate natural gifts—reason, speech, writing, beauty, and stature—from preference, which is the capacity to acquire true beliefs and virtues and thereby attain salvation; these gifts call for gratitude and monotheism.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r6.anchor: والأقرب في ذلك أن يقال : إنه تعالى فضل الإنسان على سائر الحيوانات بأمور خلقية طبيعية ذاتية مثل العقل والنطق والخط

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī sees a progression: Adam’s honor, subjugation of things, provision of good things, then preference; the following command to angels to prostrate explains the honor, with intervening verses as a digression.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r7.anchor: وقال الطيبي : قدد كرر في الآية ما ينبغي عن غاية المدح من ذكر الكرامة والتفضيل وتسخير الأشياء على سبيل الترقي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r8.claim: Another account makes honoring the gifts that enable moral responsibility and thereby expose people to a higher rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118/r8.anchor: وفيه تخصيص التكريم وكذا فيما قيل إن التكريم بالنعم التي يصح بها التكليف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.claim: Al-Kashf says the passage urges gratitude and rejection of idolatry by recalling God’s care; the preference applies to humanity as a kind and does not establish closeness to God, since its benefits include good and bad people.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.anchor: في الكشف أن الظاهر من سياق الآية أنه حث للإنسان على الشكر وعلى أن لا يشرك به تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.claim: The verse cannot settle the disputed rank of angels and humans: whether angels are included among “many” or not, the listed worldly blessings do not prove superiority in spiritual rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.anchor: وهذا التفضيل لا يراد منه عظم الدرجة وزيادة القربة عند الله تعالى وهو المتنازع فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.claim: Even if preference means the disputed rank, the verse proves it only by implication, whose authority is debated; it says humans surpass many, not whether the remainder are equal or superior.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.anchor: ثم إن على فرض أن التفضيل بالمعنى المتنازع فيه لا يدل الآية على أن الملك أفضل من البشر إلا بطريق المفهوم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r1.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads min as explanatory, so humans are preferred over all intelligent creatures; because a kind cannot outrank itself, this means angels and jinn.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r1.anchor: وجعل الطيبي من بيانية كما في قولك بذلت له العريض من جاهي أي فضلناهم على الكثيرين الذين خلقناهم من ذوي العقول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r2.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r2.claim: If min is partitive, the mention of “many” elevates those preferred over, as in the verse about raising some people by degrees.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r2.anchor: وإذا جعلت للتبعيض كان ( ممن خلقنا ) بدلا أي فضلناهم على بعض المخلوقين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r3.speaker: صاحب التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r3.claim: The author of al-Taqrīb allows that the “many” may be the angels, who are numerous among rational creatures.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r3.anchor: وإليه ينظر قول صاحب التقريب إنه يحتمل أن يراد بكثير ممن خلقنا الملائكة إذ هم كثير من العقلاء المخلوقين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī accepts the broad reading of rational creatures but rejects explanatory min as too remote and needlessly discarding the common partitive sense; contrasting “many” with some can imply majority, though not in every usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r4.anchor: وتعقب بأن ما ذكره من حمل ( من خلقنا ) على تعميم ذوي العقول مقبول فإن تفضيلهم على غير ذوي العقول حينئذ آت من طريق مفهوم الموافقة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r5.claim: The contrast “some guided, many disobedient” indicates that disobedience is the majority in that context.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r5.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى ( فمنهم مهتد وكثير منهم فاسقون )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r6.claim: When “many” is stated without an opposing group, the remainder need not be less numerous; one verse says God favored David and Solomon over many believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r6.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى ( فضلنا على كثير من عباده المؤمنين )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls the claim that specifying “many” excludes angels an unsupported argument; the verse may instead leave the preferred-over group stronger, as al-Taqrīb suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119/r7.anchor: فقوله إن صفة الكثرة إذا جعلت مخصصة الخ كلام لم يصدر عن ثبث ولهذه النكتة قال صاحب التقريب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r1.claim: Some Sunnis prefer angels to humans; this is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and reported as al-Zajjāj’s choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r1.anchor: فمنهم من ذهب إلى تفضيل الملائكة وهو مذهب ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما واختيار الزجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r2.speaker: أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r2.claim: Another Sunni position ranks human messengers first, then angel messengers, then angels generally above humans generally; it is held by Hanafis and many Shāfiʿīs and Ashʿarīs.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r2.anchor: إن الرسل من البشر أفضل مطلقا ثم الرسل من الملائكة على من سواهم من البشر والملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r3.claim: A third position gives all perfected humans, prophets or saints, precedence over angels generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r3.anchor: ومنهم من عمم تفضيل الكمل من نوع الإنسان نبيا كان أو وليا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r4.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī ranks the highest cherubic angels first, then human messengers, perfected humans, and finally angels generally above humans generally; al-Ghazālī’s writings suggest a similar view.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r4.anchor: وهذا ما عليه الإمام الرازي وبه يشعر كلام الغزالي في مواضع عديدة في كتبه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r5.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashf says neither the angel-human ranking nor the ranking of imams makes a person an innovator, provided there is no insult or violation of reverence; the imam question is more restrictive by the established Sunni view.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r5.anchor: وهذه المسئلة ومسئلة تفضيل الأئمة ليستا مما يبدع الذاهب إلى أحد طرفيهما على ما في الكشف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s abuse of those who disagree as ignorant and indecent, especially since the question is not settled by definitive proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p119#2/r6.anchor: فهذر الزمخشري على من خالفه محض جهالة إذا لم يكن بتلك الغاية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p126/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p126/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p126/r11.claim: One view says God honored humanity by creating Adam in the form of the Merciful and passing this inheritance to his descendants; another suggests humanity's honor lies in being served by other creatures and its precedence in the listed favors.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p126/r11.anchor: قيل كرمهم تعالى بأن خلق أباهم آدم على صورة الرحمن وجعل لهم ذلك بحكم الوراثة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r1.claim: One report says humans are honored because they eat with their hands, unlike animals that eat from the ground with their mouths.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: هو أنهم يأكلون بالأيدي وغير الآدمي يأكل بفيه من الأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r2.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the distinguishing honor is reason.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the honor as speech.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r4.claim: Ata identifies it as the upright, extended human stature, unlike animals bent over their faces.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء: بتعديل القامة وامتدادها والدواب منكبة على وجوهها وقيل:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r5.claim: Other interpretations are beauty of form, men's beards and women's braids, God's subjection of other things to humans, and the fact that the best community comes from them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: بحسن الصورة وقيل: الرجال باللحى والنساء بالذوائب وقيل: بأن سخر لهم سائر الأشياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r6.claim: God carries people on animals on land and ships at sea.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r6.anchor: أي: حملناهم في البر على الدواب وفي البحر على السفن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r7.claim: The good things provided are delicious food and drink.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r7.anchor: {ورزقناهم من الطيبات} يعني: لذيذ المطاعم والمشارب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r8.claim: Muqatil names butter, clarified butter, dates, and sweets as examples of the good provisions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#2/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل: السمن والزبد والتمر والحلوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r1.claim: The verse's apparent wording gives humans superiority over many created beings, not all.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r1.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنه فضلهم على كثير ممن خلقهم لا على الكل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r2.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r2.claim: Some say humans are superior to all creation except the angels.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: فضلوا على جميع الخلق إلا على الملائكة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r3.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi excepts a group of angels, including Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death, from human superiority.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: فضلوا على الخلائق كلهم إلا على طائفة من الملائكة: جبريل وميكائيل وإسرافيل وملك الموت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r4.claim: Scholars disagree over whether angels are superior to human beings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r4.anchor: وفي تفضيل الملائكة على البشر اختلاف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r5.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r5.claim: One view places humans above every creature, including all angels; it takes “many” as a possible expression for all, as in 26:221–222.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r5.anchor: فقال قوم: فضلوا على جميع الخلق وعلى الملائكة كلهم وقد يوضع الأكثر موضع الكل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r6.speaker: جابر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r6.claim: A prophetic report has angels ask for the afterlife while humans receive worldly life; God says the one He created with His own hand and breathed into is not like one created by the command “Be.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث عن جابر يرفعه قال: "لما خلق الله آدم وذريته قالت الملائكة: يا رب خلقتهم يأكلون ويشربون وينكحون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r7.claim: The author concludes that ordinary believers are better than ordinary angels and elite believers better than elite angels, citing 98:7.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r7.anchor: والأولى أن يقال: عوام المؤمنين أفضل من عوام الملائكة وخواص المؤمنين أفضل من خواص الملائكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra says a believer is more honored to God than the angels who are near Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p108#3/r8.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة أنه قال: "المؤمن أكرم على الله من الملائكة الذين عنده"

QASHANI:17:70/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:70/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:70/r1.claim: God dignifies Adam's children with speech, discernment, intellect, and knowledge.

QASHANI:17:70/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:70/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:70/r2.claim: Land and sea signify bodies and spirits; God enables people to travel both in pursuit of worldly and spiritual needs, combining them and rising beyond them toward perfection.
QASHANI:17:70/r2.anchor: يسرنا لهم أسباب المعاش والمعاد بالسير في طلبها فيهما

QASHANI:17:70/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:70/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:70/r3.claim: On one reading, humans receive uniquely compounded good things and are favored over many creatures, excluding the sanctified beings; prophets' superiority over the nearest angels comes from divine knowledge entrusted through their gathered unity, not merely from being human, as 2:30 indicates.
QASHANI:17:70/r3.anchor: وأما أفضلية بعض الناس كالأنبياء على الملائكة المقربين فليست من جهة كونهم بني آدم

QASHANI:17:70/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:70/r4.speaker: قيل
QASHANI:17:70/r4.claim: A cited couplet says that though outwardly a son of Adam, the speaker contains a meaning that testifies to divine fatherhood; another says the speaker sees God through God's eye and answers that only God remains.
QASHANI:17:70/r4.anchor: وإني وإن كنت ابن آدم صورة فلي فيه معنى شاهد بأبوتي

QASHANI:17:70/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:70/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:70/r5.claim: Alternatively, human dignity is nearness and knowledge of unity: people journey through the body-world and spirit-world to perfection, receive pure knowledge and gnosis, and are favored over all creatures; the wording intensifies the universal comparison.
QASHANI:17:70/r5.anchor: بالتقريب ومعرفة التوحيد وحملناهم في بر عالم الأجساد

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r1.claim: Human honor includes beautiful form, balanced temperament and stature, reason, speech, gesture, writing, guidance, livelihood and afterlife means, and mastery of earthly crafts and causes; these gifts defy enumeration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r1.anchor: بحسن الصورة والمزاج الأعدل واعتدال القامة والتمييز بالعقل والإفهام بالنطق والإشارة والخط والتهدي

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās specifies one distinction: animals take food with their mouths, but humans raise it to their mouths with their hands.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r2.anchor: ذكره ابن عباس: وهو أن كل حيوان يتناول طعامه بفيه إلا الإنسان فإنه يرفعه إليه بيده.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r3.claim: Being carried on land and sea means being placed on mounts and ships; alternatively, God carries them by preventing the earth from swallowing them and water from drowning them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r3.anchor: على الدواب والسفن من حملته حملا إذا جعلت له ما يركبه، أو حملناهم فيهما حتى لم تخسف بهم الأرض ولم يغرقهم الماء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r4.claim: The good things provided are pleasant provisions obtained through human effort as well as without it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r4.anchor: المستلذات مما يحصل بفعلهم وبغير فعلهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r5.claim: Humanity's preference over many creatures may mean dominance and mastery, or nobility and honor.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r6.claim: The excluded class may be all angels or only their elect; not preferring an entire class does not rule out preferring some individuals, and the question remains open. Interpreting 'many' as all is strained.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:70/r6.anchor: والمستثنى جنس الملائكة عليهم الصلاة والسلام أو الخواص منهم، ولا يلزم من عدم تفضيل الجنس عدم تفضيل بعض أفراده والمسألة موضع نظر، وقد أول الكثير بالكل وفيه تعسف.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r1.claim: Humanity’s honor after the preceding signs demonstrates God’s ability to resurrect by differentiating beings that began alike.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r2.claim: The human soul is noblest among this world’s souls because it encompasses vegetative, sensory, voluntary-motion, and rational faculties and can know God and created realms.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r2.anchor: ركب جوهر الإنسان من نفس هي أشرف النفوس بما فضلها على قوى النفس النباتية

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r3.claim: The human body is also distinguished by its upright stature and ability to reach and handle things with the hand.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r3.anchor: اعتدال القامة وامتدادها والتناول باليد وغير ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r4.claim: The omitted object of “honored” makes the honor general: humans surpass clay through growth, living things through life, and living creatures through speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r4.anchor: حذف متعلق التكريم دالا على عمومه لجميع الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r5.claim: God carries people over land on animals and over sea on ships.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r5.anchor: في البر } على الدواب وغيرها { والبحر } على السفن وغيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r6.claim: God gives people pleasant fruits and foods, while animals eat only the coarse remnants.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r6.anchor: أي المستلذات من الثمرات والأقوات التي يأكل غيرهم من الحيوان قشها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r7.claim: Humans are favored in their form, knowledge that leads to felicity, and provision, yet the verse says “many” rather than all created beings.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r7.anchor: في أنفسهم بإحسان الشكل , وفي صفاتهم بالعلم المنتج لسعادة الدارين

BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r8.claim: The elect who discipline their flawed desires and attain piety and excellence are the best of creatures; the command that angels prostrate to Adam anticipates this rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p407/r8.anchor: وأما الخلص فهم أفضل الخلائق لما علمنا من معالجتهم بالإخلاص

DURR-FULL:v5p316/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r1.speaker: عروة بن رويم اللخمي
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r1.claim: A variant of a report about human honor says people ride horses and omits the wording that God breathed His spirit into Adam.
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r1.anchor: عن عروة بن رويم اللخمي عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p316/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says human dignity includes eating with the hands, whereas other creatures eat with their mouths.
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ولقد كرمنا بني آدم} قال: جعلناهم يأكلون بأيديهم

DURR-FULL:v5p316/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r3.claim: A Prophetic report identifies the special honor as eating with the fingers.
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {ولقد كرمنا بني آدم} قال: الكرامة الأكل بالأصابع

DURR-FULL:v5p316/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r4.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r4.claim: Whoever sees an afflicted person and praises God for sparing him and favoring him is protected from that affliction, whatever it is.
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r4.anchor: عن عمر رضي الله عنه قال: ما من رجل يرى مبتلى فيقول: الحمد لله الذي عافاني مما ابتلاك به

DURR-FULL:v5p316/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says God selected the highest heaven, then humanity, Arabs, Mudar, Quraysh, and Banu Hashim, and chose Muhammad from them as the best of the best.
DURR-FULL:v5p316/r5.anchor: عن عمر رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله خلق السموات سبعا فاختار العليا منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.claim: This parenthesis recalls God's favor to all and summarizes the preceding discourse; descriptions apply to humankind as a type.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.anchor: اعتراض جاء بمناسبة العبرة والمنة على المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.claim: The five favors are dignity, land transport, sea transport, good provisions, and superiority over many creatures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.anchor: وقد جمعت الآية خمس منن : التكريم ، وتسخير المراكب في البر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.claim: Dignity makes people precious rather than abject in appearance, cleanliness, dress, comfort, eating, foresight, self-awareness, knowledge, craft, and civilization.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.anchor: فإن جميع الحيوان لا يعرف النظافة ولا اللباس ولا ترفيه المضجع والمأكل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās illustrates dignity by people lifting food and water to their mouths with fingers or utensils, unlike animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.anchor: وقد مثل ابن عباس للتكريم بأن الإنسان يأكل بأصابعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.claim: Land transport means riding mounts that God subjected and taught people to use.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.anchor: والحمل : الوضع على المركب من الرواحل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.claim: Sea carrying means being inside a ship, a conventional metaphor from riding; God inspired ships, sails, and oars, as al-Ḥāqqa 69:11 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.anchor: وأما الحمل في البحر فهو الحصول في داخل السفينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r1.claim: Good provisions include knowledge of appealing foods and benefits; humans eat more varied fare than animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r1.anchor: ألهم الإنسان أن يطعم ما يشاء مما يروق له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r2.claim: The intended superiority is observable: human reason and ingenuity allow mastery over earthly creatures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r2.anchor: فالمراد به التفضيل المشاهد لأنه موضع الامتنان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r3.claim: Dignity concerns worth in itself; superiority concerns distinction through reason, judgment, knowledge, and sciences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r3.anchor: والفرق بين التفضيل والتكريم بالعموم والخصوص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r4.claim: Comparison with unseen angels or jinn is not intended; revelation establishes rankings. Ibn ʿĀshūr rebukes al-Zamakhsharī for forcing Muʿtazilī polemic into the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r4.anchor: فليست بمقصودة هنا وإنما تعرف بأدلة توقيفية من قبل الشريعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r5.claim: “Many” deliberately limits the claim: some creatures may equal or exceed humans; revelation explains what it does and silence should not be speculated about.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r5.anchor: مراد منه التقييد والاحتراز والتعليم الذي لا غرور فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r6.claim: The indefinite absolute object tafḍīlan conveys greatness: God favored humans greatly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p165/r6.anchor: في قوله : { تفضيلا } لإفادة ما في التنكير من التعظيم

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ata says God began with kindness before obedience, answering before supplication, and giving before request, meeting every need so people would belong to the One who owns all.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ابتداهم بالبر قبل الطاعات ، وبالإجابة قبل الدعاء ، وبالعطاء قبل السؤال

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r2.claim: Junayd says humanity was honored through understanding God.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : كرمنا بني آدم بالفهم عن الله

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r3.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says humanity was honored through divine address in commands and prohibitions.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : كرمنا بني آدم بالمخاطبات بالأمر والنهي

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r4.claim: Some say humanity was honored through a well-formed body and upright stature.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كرمنا بني آدم بتقويم الخلقة واستواء القامة

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r5.claim: Some say humanity was honored through intermediaries and messengers.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : كرمنا بني آدم بالوسائط والرسل

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r6.claim: An anonymous saying names humanity's allotted portion or created form as the honor.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : كرمنا بني آدم بالحظ ، وقيل : كرمنا بني آدم بالخلق

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r7.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r7.claim: Al-Husayn says humanity was honored by being held in God's grasp and directly addressed by Him.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r7.anchor: وقال الحسين : كرمنا بني آدم بالكون في القبضة ، ومكافحة الخطاب

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r8.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r8.claim: Al-Wasiti says all humanity, believers and unbelievers, received honor, Adam was specially elected, and the universe was subjected so people could devote themselves to worship.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r8.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : أفرد آدم بالاصطفاء وافرد بني آدم بقوله : ﴿ كرمنا بني آدم ﴾ يدخل فيه الكافر

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r9.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r9.claim: Jaʿfar says humanity was honored with gnosis.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r9.anchor: قال جعفر : كرمنا بني آدم بالمعرفة

SULAMI:v1p391#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r10.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r10.claim: When asked about the honor, Dhu al-Nun says it was humanity's beautiful voice.
SULAMI:v1p391#2/r10.anchor: وسئل ذو النون عن قوله : ﴿ ولقد كرمنا بني آدم ﴾ . قال : بحسن الصوت

SULAMI:v1p392/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p392/r1.claim: An inward reading makes land the self and sea the heart: carrying a person in the self honors them with the light of divine support, while mere planning without that light soon brings ruin.
SULAMI:v1p392/r1.anchor: معنى البر النفس ، ومعنى البحر القلب ، فمن حمله في النفس فقد أكرمه بنور التأييد

SULAMI:v1p392/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p392/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti interprets land as outward attributes God manifests and sea as hidden realities.
SULAMI:v1p392/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله في قوله : ﴿ وحملناهم في البر والبحر ﴾ قال : البر ما أظهر من النعوت

SULAMI:v1p392/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p392/r3.claim: Another reading associates land and sea with separation and union in witnessing divine support.
SULAMI:v1p392/r3.anchor: وقيل : في مشاهدة أيده فصمت الوقتين الفصل والوصل وهو البر والبحر

SULAMI:v1p392/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p392/r4.claim: Abu Uthman says wholesome provision means lawful provision.
SULAMI:v1p392/r4.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : الرزق الطيب هو الحلال

SULAMI:v1p392/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392/r5.speaker: إبراهيم الخواص
SULAMI:v1p392/r5.claim: Ibrahim al-Khawwas says wholesome provision consists of permitted things.

SULAMI:v1p392/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
SULAMI:v1p392/r6.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak identifies wholesome provision as the worker's written deeds when performed sincerely.
SULAMI:v1p392/r6.anchor: قال عبد الله بن المبارك : كتب يد العامل إذا نصح

SULAMI:v1p392/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392/r7.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p392/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh says wholesome provision is what comes without asking or personal expectation.
SULAMI:v1p392/r7.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : الرزق الطيب ما يفتح على الإنسان من غير سؤال

SULAMI:v1p392#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r1.claim: Abu Uthman says humanity was preferred over all creatures through gnosis.
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : فضلناهم بالمعرفة على جميع الخلائق

SULAMI:v1p392#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r2.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r2.claim: Abu Hafs says humanity was preferred by being shown the faults of its own self.
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو حفص : فضلناهم بأن بصرناهم عيوب أنفسهم

SULAMI:v1p392#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r3.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r3.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad says humanity was preferred with discernment and preservation.
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r3.anchor: قال فضيل بن عياض : فضلناهم بالتمييز والحفظ

SULAMI:v1p392#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r4.claim: Junayd, as related by Ibn al-Furahi, says humanity was preferred through accurate spiritual insight.
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r4.anchor: وحكى ابن الفرحي عن الجنيد رحمه الله تعالى قال : فضلناهم بإصابة الفراسة

SULAMI:v1p392#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r5.speaker: السياري
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r5.claim: Al-Sayyari says scholars are preferred over the ignorant through knowledge of God and His rulings.
SULAMI:v1p392#2/r5.anchor: وقال السياري : فضلنا العلماء على الجهال بالعلم بالله وأحكامه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r1.claim: We honored means God endowed humanity with dignity and excellence, not wealth, as a fine garment is called noble for its qualities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r1.anchor: كرمنا تضعيف كرم، فالمعنى: جعلنا لهم كرما، أي شرفا وفضلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r2.claim: The verse lists human distinctions; animals and jinn are the many less-favored creatures, while angels are outside that group.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية، عدد الله تعالى فيها على بني آدم ما خصهم به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r3.claim: Humans carry themselves on land and sea by intention, purpose, and planning, unlike other animals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r3.anchor: وحملهم في البر والبحر، مما لا يصلح لحيوان سوى بني آدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r4.claim: Human provision is broader because people earn money, wear clothes, and prepare foods; provision is anything beneficial.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r4.anchor: لأنهم يكسبون المال خاصة دون الحيوان، ويلبسون الثياب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r5.speaker: جماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r5.claim: A group cites eating with hands, and another elevated sight and upright walking, as human distinctions; the author calls this inadequate because animals excel in other traits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r5.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن جماعة أنهم قالوا: «التفضيل» هو أن يأكل بيديه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r6.claim: True honor lies in intellect, by which humans know God, understand revelation, and reach bliss.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r6.anchor: وإنما التكريم والتفضيل بالعقل الذي يملك به الحيوان كله، وبه يعرف الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r7.claim: One group infers angels outrank humans because they are excluded from the many over whom humans are favored.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p472#2/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هذه الآية تقضي بفضل الملائكة على الإنس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p473/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p473/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p473/r9.claim: The verse does not require angelic superiority; angels may be superior or equal, and their superiority is established elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p473/r9.anchor: وهذا غير لازم من الآية بل التفضيل بين الإنس والجن لم تعن به الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r1.claim: Karramnā is more emphatic than akramnā.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r1.anchor: أي فضلناهم قال أبو عبيدة وكرمنا اشد مبالغة من أكرمنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r2.claim: Humans are favored over creation except certain leading angels; on this view, the favored humans are believers, favored by faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r2.anchor: أحدها أنهم فضلوا على سائر الخلق غير طائفة من الملائكة جبريل وميكائيك وإسرافيل وملك الموت وأشباههم قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r3.claim: Humans are favored because they eat with their hands, unlike other animals that eat with their mouths.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أن سائر الحيوان يأكل بفيه إلا ابن آدم فانه يأكل بيده رواه ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r4.claim: Some commentators say the favor is eating by hand and the cleanliness of human food, unlike jinn who eat bones and dung.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين المراد بهذا التفضيل أكلهم بأيديهم ونظافة ما يقتاتونه اذ الجن يقتاتون العظام والروث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r5.claim: Another view attributes human favor to reason.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r5.anchor: والثالث فضلوا بالعقل روي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r6.claim: Another view attributes human favor to speech and discernment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r7.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r7.claim: Another view attributes human favor to upright, elongated stature.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r7.anchor: والخامس بتعديل القامة وامتدادها قاله عطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r8.claim: Another view says humans are favored because Muḥammad was made one of them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r8.anchor: والسادس بأن جعل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم قاله محمد بن كعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r9.claim: Another view attributes human favor to worldly foods and pleasures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r9.anchor: والسابع فضلوا بالمطاعم واللذات في الدنيا قاله زيد بن أسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r10.speaker: يمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r10.claim: Another view attributes human favor to beauty of form.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r11.claim: Another view attributes human favor to mastery over other creatures and their subjection to humans.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r11.anchor: والتاسع بتسليطهم على غيرهم من الخلق وتسخير سائر الخلق لهم قاله محمد بن جرير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r12.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r12.claim: Another view attributes human favor to being addressed with commands and prohibitions.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r13.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r13.claim: Another view says men were given beards and women long locks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r13.anchor: والحادي عشر بأن جعلت اللحى للرجال والذوائب للنساء ذكره الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r14.claim: Although some people are disgraced unbelievers, universal honor can mean God treated all humanity as honored through abundant blessings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r14.anchor: احدهما أنه عامل الكل معاملة المكرم بالنعم الوافرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r15.claim: Alternatively, the description applies collectively because some humans possess the honored quality, as in 3:110.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r15.anchor: انه لما كان فيهم من هو بهذه الصفة أجرى الصفة على جماعتهم كقوله كنتم خيرة أمة أخرجت للناس آل عمران 110

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r16.claim: People are carried on moist backs—camels, horses, mules, and donkeys—on land, and on dry boards, ships, at sea.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r16.anchor: و في البحر على أعواد يابسة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r17.claim: Some explain the good provisions as lawful food.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r17.anchor: ورزقناهم من الطيبات فيه قولان أحدهما الحلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r18.claim: Others explain the good provisions as food pleasant to taste.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r19.claim: A literal reading of “many whom We created” means humans were not favored over every creature; Ibn ʿAbbās’s account exempts some angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r19.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما انه على لفظه وأنهم لم يفضلوا على سائر المخلوقات وقد ذكرنا عن ابن عباس انهم فضلوا على سائر الخلق غير طائفة من الملائكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r20.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r20.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p62#2/r20.claim: Others say angels are superior to humans.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r1.claim: Arabic can use “most” or “many” to mean all; thus the verse can say humanity was favored over all creation, as in 26:223.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r1.anchor: والثاني أن معناه وفضلناهم على جميع من خلقنا والعرب تضع الأكثر والكثير في موضع الجمع كقوله يلقون السمع وأكثرهم كاذبون الشعراء 223

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r2.claim: The Prophet said that the believer is more honored by God than the angels who are near Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p64/r2.anchor: وقد روى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انه قال المؤمن أكرم على الله عز وجل من الملائكة الذين عنده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r1.claim: God honors humanity by creating people in the best form: upright on two feet, eating with their hands, and equipped with senses and reason to distinguish benefits and harms in worldly and religious matters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r1.anchor: في خلقه لهم على أحسن الهيئات وأكملها (4) كما قال: {لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r2.claim: God carries people on land by livestock such as camels, horses, and mules, and at sea in large and small ships.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r2.anchor: أي: على الدواب من الأنعام والخيل والبغال، وفي "البحر" أيضا على السفن الكبار والصغار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r3.claim: God provides wholesome crops, fruit, meat, milk, varied pleasant foods and colors, fine sights, and fine clothing, made locally or brought from distant regions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97/r3.anchor: أي: من زروع وثمار، ولحوم وألبان، من سائر أنواع الطعوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r1.claim: Humans are favored above other animals and many other created kinds; Ibn Kathir cites this verse as evidence that humans as a kind rank above angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r1.anchor: وقد استدل بهذه الآية على أفضلية جنس البشر على جنس الملائكة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r2.claim: In a report sent without a Companion link, angels ask why humans receive worldly enjoyment; God answers that righteous descendants He created with His hand are not like beings created by the command 'Be.' Ibn Kathir notes a connected version exists.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r2.anchor: قالت الملائكة: يا ربنا، إنك أعطيت بني آدم الدنيا، يأكلون منها ويتنعمون،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r3.claim: A connected report repeats the angels' request for an afterlife reward and God's distinction between righteous descendants made by His hand and beings created by command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الملائكة قالت: يا ربنا، أعطيت بني آدم الدنيا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r4.claim: Another report says the angels contrasted their worship with human eating, drinking, clothing, marriage, riding, sleep, and rest; God distinguished the human He formed by hand and breathed into from one created by command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r4.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الملائكة قالوا: ربنا، خلقتنا وخلقت بني آدم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r5.claim: A very unusual report says no being is dearer to God on Judgment Day than Adam's child; it adds that angels are compelled, like the sun and moon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p97#2/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما شيء أكرم على الله يوم القيامة من ابن آدم". قيل: يا رسول الله ولا الملائكة؟

JISHUMI:v6p4260/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4260/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4260/r5.claim: Takrim and ikram both mean honoring, but takrim conveys repetition or abundance, while ikram is bestowing blessings as an act of honor.
JISHUMI:v6p4260/r5.anchor: التكريم والإكرام سواء في المعنى، وهما من الكرامة إلا أن التكريم يدل على التكرير والتكثير

JISHUMI:v6p4264/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4264/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4264/r1.claim: Karamna signals blessing but not preference, so faḍḍalna clarifies the distinction; alternatively, honor concerns worldly gifts and preference afterlife gifts, or honor enables moral responsibility while preference offers higher ranks in the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v6p4264/r1.anchor: فجوابنا: أن (كرمنا) ينبئ عن الإنعام ولا ينبئ عن التفضيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r1.claim: Views of human honor include reason, speech, discernment, writing, fine appearance and stature, managing life, dominion over earthly things, or eating with fingers; al-Rashīd demonstrates this after Abū Yūsuf cites Ibn ʿAbbās.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r1.anchor: كرمه الله بالعقل ، والنطق ، والتمييز ، والخط ، والصورة الحسنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r2.claim: The author says كثير excludes angels, whose higher standing distinguishes them, and condemns the Mujabbira for claiming humans outrank angels and fabricating traditions for this view.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p635#2/r2.anchor: هو ما سوى الملائكة وحسب بني آدم تفضيلا أن ترفع عليهم الملائكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r1.claim: The author rejects a story in which angels request worldly pleasures and God promises the afterlife, as a fabricated report of human superiority.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r1.anchor: قالت الملائكة : ربنا إنك أعطيت بني آدم الدنيا يأكلون منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r2.claim: The author rejects as fabricated the attribution to Abū Hurayra that a believer is more honored to God than angels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r2.anchor: ورووا عن أبي هريرة أنه قال : لمؤمن أكرم على الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r3.claim: The author rejects interpreting كثيرا as all created beings, which would prefer humans over angels; he calls this strained interpretation hostility to the heavenly assembly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p637/r3.anchor: بمعنى ( جميع ) في هذه الآية ، وخذلوا حتى سلبوا الذوق

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r1.claim: Humanity is honored through God's beneficence toward people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r2.claim: Humanity is honored by being given reason and discernment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r2.anchor: كرمناهم بأن جعلنا لهم عقولا وتمييزا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r3.claim: Humanity is honored in that the best community brought forth for people comes from it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r3.anchor: بأن جعلنا منهم خير أمة أخرجت للناس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r4.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r4.claim: Humans eat and drink with their hands, while other creatures take food with their mouths.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r4.anchor: الرابع : بأن يأكلوا ما يتناولونه من الطعام والشراب بأيديهم , وغيرهم يتناوله بفمه , قاله الكلبي ومقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r5.claim: Another honor is that humans receive commands and prohibitions.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r6.claim: Human honor also consists in speech and writing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r7.claim: God honored humanity by subjecting all creation to people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r7.anchor: كرمناهم بأن سخرنا جميع الخلق لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r8.claim: Ṭayyibāt means the things God made lawful.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r9.claim: Ṭayyibāt may mean food and drink people find wholesome.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r10.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r10.claim: It may mean a worker's earnings when they produce benefit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r10.anchor: الثالث : أنه كسب العامل إذا نفع , قاله سهل بن عبد الله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r11.claim: Human superiority over many creatures may be through dominance and ascendancy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r12.claim: It may be through reward and recompense.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r13.claim: It may be through preservation and discernment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p257/r14.claim: It may be through attaining insight or physiognomic perception.

MUQATIL:17:70-71/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:70-71/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:70-71/r1.claim: Humanity is honored above other animals, though not angels, by eating and drinking with hands while animals and birds use their mouths.
MUQATIL:17:70-71/r1.anchor: فضلناهم على غيرهم من الحيوان غير الملائكة حين أكلوا وشربوا بأيديهم

MUQATIL:17:70-71/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:70-71/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:70-71/r2.claim: People travel on mounts over land and ships at sea and receive good provisions beyond those of animals; the stated distinction is eating with hands.
MUQATIL:17:70-71/r2.anchor: على الرطب، يعني الدواب، { و } حملناهم في { والبحر } ، على اليابس، يعني السفن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r1.claim: Human dignity includes intellect, speech, writing, beauty, upright stature, managing worldly and religious affairs, control of things, and eating with the hands.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r1.anchor: بالعقل والنطق والخط والصورة الحسنة والقامة المعتدلة وتدبير أمر المعاش والمعاد والاستيلاء وتسخير الأشياء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains human honor as having fingers with which people eat; the report says al-Rashīd put away the spoons and ate with his fingers after Abū Yūsuf cited it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r2.anchor: جاء في تفسير حدك ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قوله تعالى ولقد كرمنا بنى آدم جعلنا لهم أصابع يأكلون بها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r3.claim: God carries people over land on riding animals and over sea in ships.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r3.anchor: ﴿ وحملناهم في البر ﴾ على الدواب ﴿ والبحر ﴾ على السفن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r4.claim: Ṭayyibāt means either delicious things or what people have earned with their own hands.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r4.anchor: ﴿ ورزقناهم من الطيبات ﴾ باللذيذات أو بما كسبت ايديهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r5.claim: The preference over 'many' can mean all, as in other Qur'anic usages; al-Ḥasan says it means all, and al-Kashshāf notes that 'most' can mean everyone.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r5.anchor: ﴿ وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا ﴾ أي على الكل كقوله وأكثرهم كاذبون قال الحسن أي كلهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r6.speaker: النبي
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r6.claim: A prophetic report says the believer is more honored by God than the angels.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r6.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام المؤمن أكرم على الله من الملائكة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r7.claim: Angels have intellect without desire and animals desire without intellect; humans have both, so one whose intellect masters desire outranks angels, while one ruled by desire is worse than beasts.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r7.anchor: وهذا لأنهم مجبولون على الطاعة ففيهم عقل بلا شهوة وفي البهائم شهوة بلا عقل وفي الآدمى كلاهما

NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r8.claim: Humans are honored because all other creatures were created for them, while humans were created for God.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p295/r8.anchor: ولأنه خلق الكل لهم وخلقهم لنفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r1.claim: After warnings, the verse also sets out God’s blessings on humanity.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r1.anchor: لما ذكر من الترهيب ما ذكر بين النعمة عليهم أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r2.claim: The doubled verb karramnā means granting nobility and distinction, not wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r2.anchor: «كرمنا» تضعيف كرم أي جعلنا لهم كرما أي شرفا وفضلا

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r3.claim: Human honor includes upright stature and good form, deliberate transport over land and sea, and special provision of foods, drink, and clothing; humans earn wealth and prepare composite dishes unlike other animals.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r3.anchor: وهذه الكرامة يدخل فيها خلقهم على هذه الهيئة في امتداد القامة وحسن الصورة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r4.speaker: جماعة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r4.claim: A group cited by al-Tabari says the distinction is that humans eat with their hands while other animals eat with their mouths.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r4.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن جماعة أن التفضيل هو أن يأكل بيده وسائر الحيوان بالفم

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil also give eating with the hand as the distinction.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r5.anchor: وهو قول الكلبي ومقاتل ذكره الماوردي

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says humanity was honored with speech and discernment.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r7.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r7.claim: ʿAta says humanity was honored with balanced, extended stature.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r8.speaker: يمان
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r8.claim: Yaman says humanity was honored with beautiful form.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says humanity was honored by having Muhammad among them.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r9.anchor: محمد بن كعب: بأن جعل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r10.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r10.claim: Al-Tabari says humanity was distinguished by dominion over other creatures and their subjection to people.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r10.anchor: وقال محمد بن جرير الطبري: بتسليطهم على سائر الخلق، وتسخير سائر الخلق لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r11.claim: Other views identify speech and writing, or understanding and discernment, as the distinction.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r11.anchor: وقيل: بالكلام والخط. وقيل: بالفهم والتمييز

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r12.claim: The author’s preferred basis of human distinction is reason, the foundation of moral responsibility: through it people know God, understand revelation, reach bliss, and affirm messengers; because reason alone is insufficient, God sent messengers and books. He compares law to the sun and reason to the eye.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r12.anchor: والصحيح الذي يعول عليه أن التفضيل إنما كان بالعقل الذي هو عمدة التكليف

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r13.claim: Some animals surpass humans in particular traits, such as a horse’s speed, an elephant’s strength, a lion’s courage, and a rooster’s noble bearing, but humanity’s central distinction is reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70/r13.anchor: وقد جعل الله في بعض الحيوان خصالا يفضل بها ابن آدم أيضا كجري الفرس وسمعه وإبصاره

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r1.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r1.claim: A group argues that the verse implies angels outrank humans and jinn because 4:172 exempts the nearest angels from servitude.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r1.anchor: ولا الملائكة المقربون [النساء: 171]. وهذا غير لازم من الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r2.claim: The inference is not necessary: this verse compares people with animals and perhaps jinn, whereas angels lie outside the group under discussion; it leaves open whether angels are better, worse, or equal.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r2.anchor: وهذا غير لازم من الآية، بل التفضيل فيها بين الإنس والجن

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r3.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r3.claim: Some avoid discussing whether angels outrank humans or whether prophets outrank one another, citing a report not to compare prophets or prefer the Prophet to Jonah.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r3.anchor: وقد تحاشى قوم من الكلام في هذا كما تحاشوا من الكلام في تفضيل بعض الأنبياء على بعض

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r4.claim: The report is not a sound basis for silence, since the Qur’an explicitly ranks prophets; the matter was discussed in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r4.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لوجود النص في القرآن في التفضيل بين الأنبياء

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r5.claim: Muqatil says “wholesome things” are tasty foods such as ghee, honey, butter, dates, and sweets, while other creatures subsist on fodder and bones.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: السمن والعسل والزبد والتمر والحلوى

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r6.claim: Human superiority over beasts, livestock, wild animals, and birds includes mastery, reward, protection, discernment, and insight.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r6.anchor: أي على البهائم والدواب والوحش والطير بالغلبة والاستيلاء، والثواب والجزاء والحفظ والتمييز

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r7.claim: The verse refutes a report attributed to ʿAisha that one should deprive oneself of tasty food because Satan runs through the veins with its strength; the author says it has no basis and authentic Sunnah contradicts it.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r7.anchor: هذه الآية ترد ما روي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r8.speaker: الصوفية
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r8.claim: Some Sufis use that report to justify avoiding wholesome foods.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r8.anchor: وبه يستدل كثير من الصوفية في ترك أكل الطيبات

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r9.speaker: سهل
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan al-Tusi relates that Sahl lived for a period on nabq leaves and spent three years eating thin fig leaves.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r9.anchor: وقد حكى أبو حامد الطوسي قال: كان سهل يقتات ورق النبق مدة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r10.speaker: ذو النون
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r10.claim: Ibrahim ibn al-Banna relates that Dhu al-Nun refused a companion’s salt and bread, saying the finely ground salt would prevent success, and subsisted on a little barley meal.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r10.anchor: وذكر إبراهيم بن البنا قال: صحبت ذا النون من إخميم إلى الإسكندرية

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r11.speaker: أبو يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r11.claim: Abu Yazid says he ate none of the food other people eat for forty years.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r11.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد: ما أكلت شيئا مما يأكله بنو آدم أربعين سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r12.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r12.claim: The scholars say such self-imposed deprivation should not be practiced: God honored humans with wheat and reserved its husks for livestock, and subsisting on bran competes with animals; barley and coarse salt can harm health, while refusing suitable food opposes divine wisdom, law, and reason. The body is a mount that must be cared for.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r12.anchor: قال علماؤنا: وهذا مما لا يجوز حمل النفس عليه لأن الله تعالى أكرم الآدمي بالحنطة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r13.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r13.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham ate butter, honey, and fine bread, saying that when they had food they ate like men and when they lacked it they endured like men.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r13.anchor: وروي عن إبراهيم بن أدهم أنه اشترى زبدا وعسلا وخبز حوارى

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r14.speaker: الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r14.claim: Al-Thawri ate meat, grapes, and fālūdhaj, then rose to pray; similar examples from the early Muslims are numerous.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#2/r14.anchor: وكان الثوري يأكل اللحم والعنب والفالوذج ثم يقوم إلى الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:70#3/r1.claim: The author calls the reported ascetic deprivation an excess in religion, if the reports are sound, and links it to the statement that monasticism was invented rather than prescribed.

MAJAZ:v1p385/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p385/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p385/r2.claim: كرمنا means honored; it is more emphatic in honoring than أكرمنا.
MAJAZ:v1p385/r2.anchor: «ولقد كرمنا بني آدم» (70) أي أكرمنا إلا أنها أشد مبالغة فى الكرامة

RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.claim: The verse gathers four kinds of divine favor that distinguish human beings; the first is their special honor.
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى في هذه الآية أربعة أنواع

RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.claim: The human being combines soul and body; the human soul is the noblest soul and the human body the noblest body in the lower world.
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.anchor: فالنفس الإنسانية أشرف النفوس الموجودة في العالم السفلي

RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.claim: The human soul shares nutrition, growth, reproduction, sensation, and voluntary movement with plant and animal life, but uniquely has a rational faculty that knows realities and receives knowledge of God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.anchor: النفس الإنسانية مختصة بقوة أخرى وهي القوة العاقلة المدركة لحقائق الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.claim: The rational faculty surpasses bodily and animal powers; Razi points to twenty arguments he gave under the verse about God as the Light of the heavens and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.anchor: ذكرنا هناك عشرين وجها في بيان أن القوة العقلية أجل وأعلى من القوة الجسمية

RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says, in a report transmitted by Maymun ibn Mihran, that humans alone eat with their hands while other creatures eat with their mouths.
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.anchor: روى ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r6.speaker: أبو يوسف
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r6.claim: At a meal hosted by al-Rashid, Abu Yusuf cites the saying attributed to his grandfather that God honored humans by giving them fingers to eat with, prompting the caliph to put away spoons.

RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v21p10#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies human honor with speech and discernment; Razi explains that human beings can communicate all they know, unlike other animals.

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r1.claim: Human beings can define and convey what they know, while other animals cannot give a full account of inward pain or pleasure; this capacity defines rational speech.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r1.anchor: فهو الإنسان ، فإنه يمكنه تعريف غيره كل ما عرفه

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r2.claim: A mute person remains included because gestures and writing convey meaning; a parrot's limited imitation does not amount to complete communication.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r2.anchor: ظهر أن الإنسان الأخرس داخل في هذا الوصف

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r3.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r3.claim: Ata's view is that human beings are honored by their upright, extended stature.

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r4.claim: Height by itself cannot explain human distinction, since trees are taller; intellect and sensory and motor powers must also be considered.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r4.anchor: لأن الأشجار أطور من قامة الإنسان بل ينبغي أن يشترط فيه شرط

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r5.speaker: بيان
