RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r5.claim: Bayan says the honor is the beauty of human form and cites God's shaping of people and praise of human creation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r5.anchor: قال بيان بحسن الصورة ، والدليل عليه

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r6.claim: Razi depicts the eye's carefully arranged dark and light rings as one example of the beauty of the human body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r6.anchor: فتأمل عضوا واحدا من أعضاء الإنسان وهو العين فخلق الحدقة سوداء

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r7.claim: Some identify writing as a distinctive honor granted to humanity.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم من كرامات الآدمي أن آتاه الله الخط

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r8.claim: Writing lets later scholars preserve and expand earlier learning, so sciences, virtues, and religious and intellectual investigations develop cumulatively.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r8.anchor: ويضم كل متأخر مباحث كثيرة إلى علم المتقدمين كثرت العلوم

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r9.claim: The Quran associates this full honor of writing with God's teaching by the pen and teaching humanity what it did not know.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r9.anchor: بالقلم * علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r10.claim: The four simple elements serve human beings: earth is a nurturing home, water supports drinking and agriculture, air sustains life and disperses decay, and fire cooks, lights, and warms.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r10.anchor: أما الأرض فهي لنا كالأم الحاضنة

RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r11.claim: The sea also serves human beings with fresh meat, ornaments, and ships sailing through it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p11/r11.anchor: سخر البحر لنأكل منه لحما طريا

RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r1.claim: The cited poem says that a person seeking winter fruit finds it in the fire of winter, illustrating fire's benefits in darkness and cold.

RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r2.claim: The upper atmospheric phenomena, minerals, plants, and animals together serve humanity, which presides over and benefits from the world as a ruler over a populated settlement.
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r2.anchor: هذا العالم بأسره جار مجرى قرية معمورة أو خان معد

RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r3.claim: Creatures fall into four classes: intellect without appetite (angels), appetite without intellect (beasts), neither (plants and inanimate things), and both (humans); humans surpass beasts and inanimate beings, though angels raise a separate question.
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r3.anchor: المخلوقات تنقسم إلى أربعة أقسام إلى ما حصلت له القوة العقلية الحكمية

RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r4.claim: Of four modes of existence, God alone is eternal and everlasting; the transient world is lowest, an eternal but non-everlasting being is impossible, while humans and angels are everlasting and thus nobler than the transient world.
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r4.anchor: وإما أن لا يكون أزليا ولكنه يكون أبديا ، وهو الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r5.claim: The upper world is nobler than the lower; the human spirit belongs to the upper, holy order, and is uniquely present among the lower world's creatures.
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r5.anchor: وروح الإنسان من جنس الأرواح العلوية والجواهر القدسية

RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r6.claim: The nearest being to God is the noblest; humans approach through hearts illuminated by knowledge, tongues in remembrance, and limbs in obedience, and all their possible perfections come from God's gift.
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r6.anchor: قلبه مستنير بمعرفة الله تعالى ولسانه مشرف بذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r7.claim: God's generosity toward humanity spans creation, upbringing, and the final stage of human life, as shown by verses on the pen and God's gracious address to humanity.
RAZI-FULL:v21p12/r7.anchor: ووصف نفسه بالتكريم عند تربيته للإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r1.claim: Some say God created Adam with His own hand while creating other beings by the command Be; this expresses greater care for Adam and dignity for his descendants.
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r1.anchor: هذا التكريم معناه أنه تعالى خلق آدم بيده وخلق غيره بطريق كن فيكون

RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says people are carried over land on horses, mules, donkeys, and camels, and over sea in ships.
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في البر على الخيل والبغال والحمير والإبل

RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r3.claim: The animals, water, and ships are subjected to human use for travel, defense, warfare, and livelihood, making humanity like ruler over its dependents.
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r3.anchor: سخر هذه الدواب له حتى يركبها ويحمل عليها ويغزو ويقاتل

RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r4.claim: Humans receive the finest animal and plant foods, purified, cooked, and fully prepared for consumption.
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r4.anchor: يتغذى الإنسان منه بألطف أنواعها وأشرف أقسامها

RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r5.claim: Honor refers to natural endowments such as intellect, speech, writing, beauty, and stature; preference refers to using them to acquire true beliefs and virtuous character.
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r5.anchor: الأول هو التكريم والثاني هو التفضيل

RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r6.claim: The wording says humans are preferred over many creatures, not all; those who draw the implication identify angels as beings above humans.
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r6.anchor: فهذا يدل على أنه حصل في مخلوقات الله تعالى شيء لا يكون الإنسان مفضلا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that angels are better than humans; al-Zajjaj also adopts this view, as al-Wahidi reports.
RAZI-FULL:v21p13/r7.anchor: وهذا القول مذهب ابن عباس واختيار الزجاج على ما رواه الواحدي

RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r1.claim: The question whether prophets or angels are superior was treated at length under the command that the angels prostrate to Adam.
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r1.anchor: وقد سبق ذكر هذه المسألة بالاستقصاء في سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r2.claim: A report from Zayd ibn Aslam says angels asked why humans received worldly pleasures and asks that they receive such gifts in the afterlife; God swears that Adam's descendants, created by His hand, will not be treated like those created by Be.
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r2.anchor: روي عن زيد بن أسلم أنه قال : قالت الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra says a believer is more honored by God than the angels who are near Him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r3.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه : المؤمن أكرم على الله

RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r4.claim: Those who claim angels are categorically superior rely on an argument from the verse's implied contrast, but Razi calls this a weak proof.
RAZI-FULL:v21p14/r4.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة تمسك بدليل الخطاب

NAHHAS:v2p433/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p433/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p433/r5.claim: Humans are favored over many rather than all creation because angels are superior in obedience and have no sin.
NAHHAS:v2p433/r5.anchor: ولم يقل : على كل من خلقنا لأن الملائكة أفضل منهم لطاعتهم وأنهم لا معصية لهم

NAHHAS:v2p433/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p433/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p433/r6.claim: تفضيلا is an emphatic verbal noun.

STUDYQURAN:17:70/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r1.claim: God's honor to humanity can mean granting people authority over other creatures and making the rest of creation serve them.
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r1.anchor: According to some, God has honored the Children of Adam by granting them authority over other creatures

STUDYQURAN:17:70/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r2.claim: Distinctive human blessings include using arms and hands, intellect, discernment, speech, and the ability to know God.
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r2.anchor: Others mention various blessings given uniquely to human beings

STUDYQURAN:17:70/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r3.claim: The Quran connects human honor to God's creation of Adam with His Hands, breathing His Spirit into him, and giving him extraordinary knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r3.anchor: Human beings are carried over land by riding animals

STUDYQURAN:17:70/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r4.claim: Land transport by riding animals and sea transport by ships are divine blessings for which people should be grateful.
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r4.anchor: Human beings are carried over land by riding animals, which are mentioned elsewhere as a Divine blessing

STUDYQURAN:17:70/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r5.claim: The good things God provides refer to the various foods and drinks on earth.
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r5.anchor: The good things provided to them refer to the various kinds of food and drink provided for them on earth

STUDYQURAN:17:70/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r6.claim: Some take God's favoring humanity above many creatures to mean above all creation, including angels, as suggested by the angels' bow to Adam.
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r6.anchor: that He favored them over all that He has created

STUDYQURAN:17:70/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r7.claim: One interpretation distinguishes worldly blessings as God's honoring of humanity from spiritual or Hereafter blessings as His favoring them.
STUDYQURAN:17:70/r7.anchor: Some commentators consider God’s “honoring” the Children of Adam as referring to the worldly blessings He gives them

TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r1.claim: God honored Adam's descendants by giving them mastery over other creatures, transport on land and sea, and lawful, pleasant food and drink.

TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r2.claim: Human hands make people able to work, take food and drink, and raise them to their mouths, a capacity other creatures lack.
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r2.anchor: ذكر لنا أن ذلك تمكنهم من العمل بأيديهم، وأخذ الأطعمة والأشربة بها ورفعها بها إلى أفواههم

TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r3.claim: He says human beings are distinguished by their two hands for eating and working, unlike other creatures.
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله {ولقد كرمنا بني آدم} [الإسراء: 70] . الآية، قال: وفضلناهم في اليدين يأكل بهما

TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r4.claim: When angels asked why Adam's descendants received worldly enjoyment, God said He would not equate those created by His hands with those created by the command Be.
TAB-FULL:v14p6#3/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، في قوله: {ولقد كرمنا بني آدم} [الإسراء: 70] قال: قالت الملائكة: يا ربنا إنك أعطيت بني آدم الدنيا

TABATABAI:17:68-70/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:68-70/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:68-70/r5.claim: The honor statement both recounts extensive gifts and reproaches people for forgetting God after rescue; it concerns humanity generally, beyond the special spiritual honor of some.
TABATABAI:17:68-70/r5.anchor: الآية مسوقة للامتنان مشوبا بالعتاب كأنه تعالى لما ذكر وفور نعمه

TABATABAI:17:68-70/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:68-70/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:68-70/r6.claim: Takrīm is intrinsic, distinctive dignity, while tafḍīl is comparative extra giving; the human intellect distinguishes truth from falsehood and good from harm.
TABATABAI:17:68-70/r6.anchor: وبذلك يفترق عن التفضيل فإن التكريم معنى نفسي وهو جعله شريفا ذا كرامة في نفسه

TABATABAI:17:70/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70/r1.claim: Human invention in food, drink, clothing, housing, sex, and social organization displays intellect; other creatures' behavior remains simple and fixed.
TABATABAI:17:70/r1.anchor: وهي واقفة في موقفها المحفوظ لها يوم خلقت من غير تغير أو تحول محسوس

TABATABAI:17:70/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70/r2.claim: Humanity is honored by the intellect that distinguishes truth and falsehood, good and evil, and benefit and harm.
TABATABAI:17:70/r2.anchor: وهو العقل الذي يعرفون به الحق من الباطل والخير من الشر والنافع من الضار

TABATABAI:17:70/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70/r3.claim: Reports and commentators list speech, stature, fingers, eating by hand, writing, beauty, subduing creation, Adam's creation by God's hand, and Muhammad's descent among humanity as honors.
TABATABAI:17:70/r3.anchor: وأما ما ذكره المفسرون أو وردت به الرواية أن الذي كرمهم الله به النطق أو تعديل القامة

TABATABAI:17:70/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70/r4.claim: The author treats some listed honors as products of intellect and others as examples of comparative preference; Adam's creation and Muhammad's descent are spiritual honors beyond this verse's scope.
TABATABAI:17:70/r4.anchor: وبعضها من مصاديق التفضيل دون التكريم

TABATABAI:17:70/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70/r5.speaker: صاحب روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:70/r5.claim: The author rejects the claim that all listed traits are examples and that Ibn Atiyya wrongly restricts honor to intellect alone.
TABATABAI:17:70/r5.anchor: وقد أخطأ صاحب روح المعاني حيث قال بعد ذكر الأقوال والكل في الحقيقة على سبيل التمثيل

TABATABAI:17:70/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70/r6.claim: Being carried by ships and animals and receiving desirable foods are manifestations of divine honor, like a guest supplied transport and a generous meal.

TABATABAI:17:70#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r1.claim: Carrying people and providing good things are concrete instances underlying the general heading of divine honor.
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r1.anchor: على التكريم من قبيل عطف المصاديق المترتبة على العنوان الكلي المنتزع منها

TABATABAI:17:70#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r2.claim: Many of God's creatures means animal kinds and jinn; animals are communities like humans, as 6:38 says, while angels are outside the material cosmic order under discussion.
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r2.anchor: لا يبعد أن يكون المراد بمن خلقناهم أنواع الحيوان ذوات الشعور والجن الذي يثبته القرآن

TABATABAI:17:70#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r3.claim: Angels are luminous, non-cosmic beings outside the material comparison, so the verse's many does not include them in its comparison.
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r3.anchor: وأما الملائكة فليسوا من الموجودات الكونية الواقعة تحت تأثير النظام المادي

TABATABAI:17:70#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r4.claim: Honor is the uniquely human gift of intellect and its derivatives; preference is superiority in shared gifts, as human food, dress, homes, and society become more varied than animals'.
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r4.anchor: وأما تفضيله فبما يزيد به على غيره في الأمور المشتركة بينه وبين غيره

TABATABAI:17:70#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r5.claim: Humans elaborate common nourishment into countless cooked and uncooked foods, just as they develop drink, clothing, homes, family life, and society.
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r5.anchor: والإنسان يتغذى بذلك ويزيد عليه بما يبدعه من ألوان الغذاء المطبوخ وغير المطبوخ

TABATABAI:17:70#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r6.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r6.claim: Al-Majmaʿ offers three distinctions: honor signifies beneficence while preference signals giving; honor is worldly gifts and preference afterlife gifts; or honor enables obligation and preference is the obligation leading to higher stations.
TABATABAI:17:70#2/r6.anchor: وقال في مجمع البيان ومتى قيل إذا كان معنى التكريم والتفضيل واحدا فما معنى التكرار

TABATABAI:17:70#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r1.claim: The author rejects the claim that preference necessarily means an undeserved gift and says the other proposed distinctions lack evidence.
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r1.anchor: ففيه أنه ممنوع والتفضيل كما يصح لا عن استحقاق من المفضل كذلك يصح عن استحقاق منه لذلك

TABATABAI:17:70#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r2.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r2.claim: Al-Razi distinguishes innate gifts such as reason and speech from acquired beliefs and virtues, calling the former honor and the latter preference.
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r2.anchor: وقال الرازي في تفسيره في الفرق بينهما إن الأقرب في ذلك أن يقال

TABATABAI:17:70#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r3.claim: The author rejects assigning honor exclusively to innate gifts and preference exclusively to acquired ones because ordinary language does not support that distinction.
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r3.anchor: لكن اختصاص التكريم بالنوع الأول والتفضيل بالنوع الثاني لا يساعد عليه لغة ولا عرف

TABATABAI:17:70#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r4.claim: The verse concerns human excellence within material cosmic existence; angels' different mode of existence is outside its subject.
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r4.anchor: أن الآية ناظرة إلى الكمال الإنساني من حيث وجوده الكوني

TABATABAI:17:70#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r5.claim: Some argue that the verse implies angels outrank even the prophets because humans are preferred only over many creatures; the author replies that angels are not part of this worldly cosmic comparison.
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r5.anchor: والملائكة غير موجودين بهذا النحو من الوجود

TABATABAI:17:70#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r6.claim: Others say many means all and min is explanatory; the author rejects this as awkward and incompatible with the Arabic wording and context.
TABATABAI:17:70#3/r6.anchor: بأن المراد بالكثير في الآية الجميع ومن بيانية

TABATABAI:17:70#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r1.claim: One response says that if angels are excluded the verse is silent about their rank, or at most ranks angelic kinds above human kinds without excluding superior human prophets.
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r1.anchor: فغايه ما في الباب أن تكون الآية ساكتة عن تفضيل بني آدم على الملائكة

TABATABAI:17:70#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r2.claim: The author reiterates that this verse concerns cosmic existence, not afterlife reward, and that its partitive many means creatures other than angels, including humans, animals, and jinn.
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r2.anchor: والمراد بكثير ممن خلقنا غير الملائكة ومن تبعيضية

TABATABAI:17:70#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r3.speaker: الأشاعرة
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r3.claim: A well-known Ashʿari view, also held by Shiʿis, ranks believers above angels, not all humans, since some humans are worse than cattle; proponents cite the verse and reports that believers are dearer to God.
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r3.anchor: فالمعروف المنسوب إلى الأشاعره أن الإنسان أفضل والمراد به أفضلية المؤمنين منهم

TABATABAI:17:70#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r4.speaker: الأشاعرة
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r4.claim: One argument says a human who freely obeys despite equal capacity for sin has greater merit than an angel naturally disposed to obedience.
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r4.anchor: فالإنسان المؤمن المطيع يطيعه وهو غير ممنوع من المعصية بخلاف الملك

TABATABAI:17:70#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r5.speaker: الزجاج وابن عباس
TABATABAI:17:70#4/r5.claim: Some Ashʿaris instead rank angels above humans universally, a position attributed to al-Zajjaj and Ibn Abbas.

TABATABAI:17:70#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r1.claim: One ranking places human messengers first, then angelic messengers above all other humans and angels, then everyone else.
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r1.anchor: ومنهم من قال بأفضليه الرسل من البشر، مطلقا ثم الرسل من الملائكة على من سواهم

TABATABAI:17:70#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r2.speaker: الرازي والغزالي
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r2.claim: Another ranking puts cherubim first, human messengers second, perfected humans third, and ordinary angels above ordinary humans.
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r2.anchor: كما يقول به الإمام الرازي ونسب إلى الغزالي

TABATABAI:17:70#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r3.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that angels outrank humans, relying on the apparent limitation in the verse's many.
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r3.anchor: وذهبت المعتزلة إلى أفضلية الملائكة من البشر واستدلوا على ذلك بظاهر قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:17:70#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says angels' superiority is sufficient human honor and attacks those who read many as all to rank humans above angels, citing transmitted reports and accusing them of strained, hostile interpretation.
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r4.anchor: فقال في الكشاف في ذيل قوله تعالى { وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا } هو ما سوى الملائكة

TABATABAI:17:70#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r5.speaker: ابن عمر وأنس بن مالك وزيد بن أسلم وجابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r5.claim: The cited report says angels asked for the afterlife while Adam's descendants received worldly pleasures, and God refused to equate hand-created Adam with one made by the command Be.
TABATABAI:17:70#5/r5.anchor: رواية سؤال الملائكة أن يجعل لهم الآخرة كما جعل لبني آدم الدنيا رويت عن ابن عمر وأنس بن مالك

TABATABAI:17:66-72/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r1.claim: The report that angels asked for worldly pleasures is implausible: eating, sex, and riding are material means of human survival, while angels already possess the perfections humans seek through matter.
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r1.anchor: ومتن الرواية لا يخلو عن شيء فإن الأكل والشرب والنكاح ونحوها في الإنسان استكمالات مادية

TABATABAI:17:66-72/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r2.claim: A further argument for human superiority says obedience has greater merit when one can equally choose sin, and temptation increases the merit of restraint.
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r2.anchor: وهذا مبني على أصل عقلائي معتبر في المجتمع الإنساني وهو أن الطاعة التي هي امتثال الخطاب المولوي

TABATABAI:17:66-72/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r3.claim: Moral credit varies with capacity and impediments: abstaining from sin is not equally meritorious for someone incapable, an aged person, and a healthy young person.
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r3.anchor: فليس يستوى في امتثال النهي عن الزنا مثلا العنين والشيخ الهرم

TABATABAI:17:66-72/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r4.claim: Angels lack appetite and anger, so their obedience is compared by proponents to abstinence by the aged or impeded; under that argument humans would earn greater merit.
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r4.anchor: ولما كانت الملائكة لا سبيل لهم إلى المعصية لفقدهم غرائز الشهوة والغضب

TABATABAI:17:66-72/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r5.claim: The analogy would erase angels' merit and intrinsic worth if their obedience were merely involuntary; it cannot explain their honored nearness, sanctified dwellings, and divine commissions.
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r5.anchor: لكن الله سبحانه أقامهم مقام القرب والزلفى وأسكنهم في حظائر القدس ومنازل الأنس

TABATABAI:17:66-72/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r6.claim: Since God praised angels and entrusted them with His secrets and commands, their rank cannot be an arbitrary assignment without any fitness or deserving quality in their own being.
TABATABAI:17:66-72/r6.anchor: وهل هذا كله لإرادة منه جزافية من غير صلاحية منهم واستحقاق من ذواتهم

TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r1.claim: The Qur'an describes angels as honored, obedient servants who do not speak ahead of God; the Prophet is told to remember and worship as they do.
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r1.anchor: بل عباد مكرمون لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r2.claim: Merit lies in the servant's pure nature and sincere submission disclosed by choosing obedience; strenuous obedience by a hypocrite or diseased heart has no value.
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r2.anchor: لا قيمه للطاعه مع العلم بخباثة نفس المطيع وقبح سريرته

TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r3.claim: Angels' pure nature and worship are superior to human nature and works, which are mixed with desire, anger, hidden association, and the self; the reward humans seek is already theirs.
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r3.anchor: فالقوام الملكي أفضل من القوام الإنساني والأعمال الملكية الخالصة لوجه الله أفضل

TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r4.claim: Humans can develop gradually toward a degree of nearness and perfection beyond the angels' initial endowment; the creation of Adam and knowledge of the names support that possibility.
TABATABAI:17:66-72#2/r4.anchor: من المحتمل أن ينال عن استعداده مقاما من القرب وموطنا من الكمال فوق ما قد ناله الملك

TABATABAI:17:71/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:71/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:71/r1.claim: The angels' prostration to Adam was submission to the perfection of humanity; Adam served as their qibla, representing humankind before the angels.
TABATABAI:17:71/r1.anchor: أن السجدة إنما كان خضوعا منهم لمقام الكمال الإنساني ولم يكن آدم عليه السلام إلا قبلة لهم

TABATABAI:17:72/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:72/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
TABATABAI:17:72/r5.claim: A report from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, explains human honor through creation's preference for humans and their ability to raise food and drink to the mouth by hand.
TABATABAI:17:72/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن علي عن أبيه عليه السلام في قوله { ولقد كرمنا بني آدم } يقول فضلنا بني آدم

TABATABAI:17:72/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:72/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:72/r6.claim: The examples in the two reports are particular instances of human preference, as the first report itself concludes.
TABATABAI:17:72/r6.anchor: وما في الروايتين من قبيل ذكر بعض المصاديق والدليل عليه قوله في آخر الرواية الأولى فهذا من التفضيل

TABATABAI:17:72/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:72/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:17:72/r7.claim: A report from Jabir says everything except the human was created bent over, while the human was created upright, as an example of human distinction.
TABATABAI:17:72/r7.anchor: عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام { وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا } قال خلق كل شيء منكبا غير الإنسان خلق منتصبا

TABRISI:17:72/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:72/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:72/r7.claim: Because Iblīs complained that Adam was honored, the following passage describes honors and blessings bestowed on Adam’s descendants.
TABRISI:17:72/r7.anchor: لما تقدم قول إبليس هذا الذي كرمت علي ذكر سبحانه بعد ذلك تكرمة لبني آدم

TABRISI:17:70-72/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r1.claim: The cited praise ‘You are the best community’ illustrates applying a quality to a group on account of its members who possess it.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r1.anchor:
كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس
[آل عمران: 11]

TABRISI:17:70-72/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r2.claim: Another view includes all humans despite unbelievers because they receive worldly blessings, good forms, subjection of things, and messengers.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r2.anchor: وقيل إنما عمهم بالتكرمة مع أن فيهم الكافر المهان لأن المعنى أكرمناهم بالنعم الدنيوية

TABRISI:17:70-72/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r3.claim: A further explanation is that God treated humanity as honored, an emphatic description of His dealings with them.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه عاملناهم معاملة المكرم على وجه المبالغة في الصفة

TABRISI:17:70-72/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
TABRISI:17:70-72/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say human honor includes strength, reason, speech, and discernment.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r4.anchor: فقيل بالقوة والعقل والنطق والتمييز عن ابن عباس والضحاك

TABRISI:17:70-72/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r5.speaker: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:70-72/r5.claim: Maymūn ibn Mihrān transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that humans eat with their hands, unlike animals, which eat with their mouths.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r5.anchor: رواه ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:17:70-72/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r6.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:17:70-72/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ identifies the honor as upright, extended human stature.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r6.anchor: وقيل بتعديل القامة وامتدادها عن عطاء

TABRISI:17:70-72/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TABRISI:17:70-72/r7.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh says the honor lies in fingers with which people can do what they wish.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r7.anchor: وقيل بالأصابع يعملون بها ما يشاؤون روى ذلك جابر بن عبد الله

TABRISI:17:70-72/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
TABRISI:17:70-72/r8.claim: Ibn Jarīr says humans are honored by ruling over other creatures and having animals made subject to them.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r8.anchor: وقيل بتسليطهم على غيرهم وتسخير سائر الحيوانات لهم عن ابن جرير

TABRISI:17:70-72/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TABRISI:17:70-72/r9.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says one honor is that Muhammad belongs to humanity.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r9.anchor: وقيل بأن جعل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم عن محمد بن كعب

TABRISI:17:70-72/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r10.claim: Other proposed honors include knowing and obeying God; the author favors including all these and other blessings.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r10.anchor: وقيل بأنهم يعرفون الله ويأتمرون بأمره وقيل بجميع ذلك وغيره من النعم

TABRISI:17:70-72/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r11.claim: People are carried on land by camels, horses, mules, and donkeys, and by ships at sea; provisions include fruits and pleasures distinctive to humanity.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r11.anchor: { وحملناهم في البر والبحر } في البر على الإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير

TABRISI:17:70-72/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r12.claim: Some argue that ‘over many of what We created’ implies angels are superior to prophets because humanity surpasses other animals and ‘many’ suggests exceptions.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r12.anchor: استدل بعضهم بهذا على أن الملائكة أفضل من الأنبياء قال لأن قوله على كثير يدل

TABRISI:17:70-72/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r13.claim: The author rejects this: preference here is varieties of worldly blessings, not comparative reward, so the verse does not establish angelic superiority.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r13.anchor: أن التفضيل ها هنا لم يرد به الثواب لأن الثواب لا يجوز التفضيل به ابتداء

TABRISI:17:70-72/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72/r14.claim: Alternatively, kathīr can rhetorically stand for all; even if partitive and about reward, angels as a class can outrank humanity while individual prophets surpass angels.
TABRISI:17:70-72/r14.anchor: أن المراد بالكثير الجميع فوضع الكثير موضع الجميع والمعنى أنا فضلناهم على من خلقنا

TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r1.claim: The author cites Suwayd ibn Abī Kāhil’s praise of people without immediate indecency or anguished impatience; it does not imply later indecency.
TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r1.anchor:
من أناس ليس في أخلاقهم
عاجل الفحش ولا سوء الجزع

TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r2.claim: To explain apparent repetition, takrīm may denote worldly gifts and tafḍīl afterlife gifts, or takrīm the means for moral duty and tafḍīl the high ranks earned through it.
TABRISI:17:70-72#2/r2.anchor: وقيل إن التكريم يتناول نعم الدنيا والتفضيل يتناول نعم الآخرة

THALABI:v6p114/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p114/r6.claim: One interpretation is that humans eat with their hands while other creatures eat with their mouths; another says human honor is reason.
THALABI:v6p114/r6.anchor: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس في قوله ولقد كرمنا بني آدم قال: كل شيء يأكل

THALABI:v6p114/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r7.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p114/r7.claim: He says God honored humans with speech and discernment.

THALABI:v6p114/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r8.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v6p114/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ identifies human honor as upright, proportioned stature.

THALABI:v6p114/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r9.speaker: يمان
THALABI:v6p114/r9.claim: Yamān says humans were honored with beautiful form.

THALABI:v6p114/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r10.speaker: محمد بن كعب
THALABI:v6p114/r10.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says humanity was honored by God making Muhammad one of them.
THALABI:v6p114/r10.anchor: محمد بن كعب: بأن جعل محمدا منهم

THALABI:v6p114/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p114/r11.claim: Another view points to men’s beards and women’s tresses as forms of distinction.

THALABI:v6p114/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r12.speaker: محمد بن جرير
THALABI:v6p114/r12.claim: Humans are honored by being empowered over other creatures and having creation subjected to them.
THALABI:v6p114/r12.anchor: محمد بن جرير: بتسليطهم على غيرهم من الخلق

THALABI:v6p114/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p114/r13.claim: Good provisions are pleasant foods and drinks; Muqātil names ghee, butter, dates, and sweets.
THALABI:v6p114/r13.anchor: ورزقناهم من الطيبات يعني لذيذ المطاعم والمشارب

THALABI:v6p114/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r14.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p114/r14.claim: He names clarified butter, butter, dates, and sweets as human provisions.

THALABI:v6p114/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r15.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p114/r15.claim: One view reads “many” as all creatures except some angels; al-Kalbī names Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, the Angel of Death, and similar angels.
THALABI:v6p114/r15.anchor: قال الكلبي: فضلوا على الخلائق كلهم غير طائفة من الملائكة

THALABI:v6p114/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p114/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p114/r16.claim: Others take “many” rhetorically as all, as in the cited verse where “most” refers to all devils.
THALABI:v6p114/r16.anchor: وقال الآخرون: المراد به جميع من خلقنا

THALABI:v6p115/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p115/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v6p115/r1.claim: Angels asked why Adam’s descendants received worldly food while angels did not; God swore not to equate those made by His hands with those created by His command Be.
THALABI:v6p115/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، في قوله تعالى ولقد كرمنا بني آدم قال: قالت: الملائكة

THALABI:v6p115/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p115/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p115/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra says a believer is more honored with God than the angels near Him.
THALABI:v6p115/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: المؤمن أكرم على الله من الملائكة الذين عنده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses honoring humanity as preferring or ennobling them, comparable to 17:62; another report says humans uniquely eat with their hands rather than their mouths.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد فضلنا (¬5)، وهو كقوله: {هذا الذي كرمت علي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says human honor consists in eating with the hands, and another attributes it to reason.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r2.anchor: كل شيء يأكل بفيه إلا ابن آدم يأكل بيديه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r3.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the distinction is speech and discernment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r4.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r4.claim: Ata says the distinction is upright, extended stature.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r5.speaker: يمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r5.claim: Yaman says the distinction is beauty of form.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r6.claim: Humans are carried at sea in ships and on land by camels, horses, mules, and donkeys.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r6.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد في البحر على السفن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r7.claim: Good provisions mean fruits, grains, and livestock; Muqatil specifies clarified butter, butter, and sweets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p401/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ورزقناهم من الطيبات} قال: يريد الثمار والحبوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r1.speaker: مكحول عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas again explains human preference by noting that animals eat with their mouths while humans eat with their hands; Ikrima gives a similar account.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r1.anchor: روى مكحول عن ابن عباس في هذا، قال: البهائم تأكل بأفواهها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r2.speaker: محمد بن جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says humanity is preferred because people are given mastery over animals and wild beasts, many of which God subjected to them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r3.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r3.claim: Al-Suddi takes the many creatures to mean animals and beasts over whom humans are preferred.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: فضلوا على البهائم والدواب والوحوش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says humans are preferred over all creatures except a group of high-ranking angels, including Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: فضلوا على الخلائق كلهم إلا (¬5) عن طائفة من الملائكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says the verse says many rather than all because angels are preferred; Adam's descendants are preferred over nonrational animals, not angels. Ata's Ibn Abbas report agrees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r5.anchor: لأن الله فضل (¬7) الملائكة (¬8)، ولكن ابن آدم مفضل على سائر الحيوانات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r6.claim: Some favor Adam's descendants over angels, citing Zayd ibn Aslam's report that God promised not to make descendants created by His hands equal to the angels addressed with Be.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r6.anchor: قالت الملائكة: ربنا إنك أعطيت بني آدم الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra says a believer is dearer to God than the angels near Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r7.anchor: قال أبو هريرة: المؤمن أكرم على الله من الملائكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r8.claim: The disagreement concerns whether righteous believers outrank angels, apart from human prophets and foremost angels; the author's companions differ, Abu Ishaq rejecting the preference, and scholars discourage extending the dispute.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p403/r8.anchor: هذه من المسائل التي لا يستحب الخوض فيها والإبلاغ

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r1.claim: Humanity is honored with reason, speech, and discernment, transported over land on camels, horses, mules, and donkeys and by sea on ships.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r1.anchor: { ولقد كرمنا } فضلنا { بني آدم } بالعقل والنطق والتمييز { وحملناهم في البر } على الإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r2.claim: Good provisions include fruits, grains, livestock, ghee, butter, and sweets; humans are preferred over beasts and wild animals.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:70-71/r2.anchor: { ورزقناهم من الطيبات } الثمار والحبوب والمواشي والسمن والزبد والحلاوى { وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا } يعني: البهائم والدواب والوحوش.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r1.speaker: الفرات بن سلمان
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r1.claim: Al-Furat reports that during a journey the Prophet told his companions to wash their hands and drink from roadside pools after some had dipped their heads into them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r1.anchor: الفرات بن سلمان، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه كانوا في سفر، فمروا ببرك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r2.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r2.claim: Some said this verse was revealed on that occasion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r2.anchor: قال يحيى: سمعت بعضهم يقول: إن هذه الآية نزلت عند ذلك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r3.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r3.claim: Hasan says human beings are favored over livestock, predatory beasts, and crawling creatures.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: فضل بنو آدم على البهائم والسباع والهوام.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r4.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r4.claim: Some explain the good provisions as bread, meat, honey, clarified butter, and similar foods and drinks, finer than the provision of animals, birds, and jinn.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p150/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {ورزقناهم من الطيبات} [الإسراء: 70] : يعني جميع رزق بني آدم: الخبز، واللحم، والعسل، والسمن،

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r1.claim: The commentary renders karam as “honor, dignity, and blessings”: it covers spiritual qualities such as nobility as well as material wealth bestowed by God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r1.anchor: kerem kavramı, İslâmî literatürde hem Allah’ın insanlara şeref, soyluluk

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r2.claim: The verse portrays humans as the creatures most favored by God’s grace, most select and valuable in the world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r2.anchor: insanı dünyada Allah’ın lutfuna en çok mazhar olmuş, en seçkin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r3.claim: Commentators explain human distinction through capacities from intellect, discernment, thought, and writing to psychological and physical traits, aesthetics, morals, stewardship, economic activity, and civilization-building.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r3.anchor: akıl, zekâ, temyiz, düşünme, yazma gibi melekelerden başlayarak çeşitli psikolojik

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r4.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r4.claim: Razi records an older debate over whether humans or angels are superior; Ibn Ashur says this verse makes no such comparison, but means humans use some creatures in various ways.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r4.anchor: Eski tefsirlerde insan mı melek mi daha üstün diye bir tartışmaya girilmişse

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r5.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur’s reading, favored by the author, is that no human–angel ranking is at issue; the point is humans’ use of other beings for their benefit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r5.anchor: burada böyle bir mukayese söz konusu olmayıp insanın bazı varlıkları çeşitli şekillerde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r6.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r6.claim: Razi locates humanity’s chief honor and superiority in intellect, the power to grasp realities as they are and reach knowledge of created realms and God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r6.anchor: insanın asıl şerefini ve diğer yaratılmışlar karşısındaki üstünlüğünü, “eşyanın gerçeklerini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r7.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r7.claim: Razi says human use of animals and constructed vehicles such as ships is distinctive; this shows humans as rulers and other beings as their subjects.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r7.anchor: Bütün bunlar, dünyamızda insanoğlunun, kendisine uyulup itaat edilen mutlak başkan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r8.claim: The Qur’an draws attention to meaningful events overlooked through daily familiarity as clear signs of divine power and wisdom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r8.anchor: Kur’an genellikle insanların hemen her gün yaşadıkları ya da çevrelerinde sürüp gittiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r9.claim: Transport aids trade and other human aims; these means, including modern travel and communication reaching into space, are divine favors and explain why the verse invites reflection on transport.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r9.anchor: İnsanların taşıma araçları kullanarak ticaret vb. konulardaki amaçlarını daha kolay

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r10.claim: Provision broadly includes everything people benefit from; “good” provision means both lawful and pleasing food and resources.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r10.anchor: “Güzel güzel rızıklar”dan maksat, hem helâl hem de hoşa giden rızıklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r11.claim: People should seek what they need lawfully and care that it is healthier, cleaner, and aesthetically better.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:70/r11.anchor: ihtiyaç duyduğu şeylerin helâlini araması yanında sağlık yönünden daha kaliteli

SAMIN-DURR:17:70/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:70/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:70/r1.claim: كرمنا is causative by gemination, from كَرُمَ (to be noble, like شرف); it does not mean generosity with money.
SAMIN-DURR:17:70/r1.anchor: عداه بالتضعيف، وهو من كرم بالضم كشرف، وليس المراد من الكرم في المال.

ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r3.claim: Human honor consists in discernment, the subjection of what is in heaven and earth, and transport over land and sea.
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r3.anchor: فضلهم بالتمييز، وبأن سخر لهم ما في السماوات والأرض وبحملهم في البر والبحر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r4.claim: God says humans were favored over many, not all, because He favored the angels; humans are favored over animals without understanding or discernment.
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r4.anchor: قال: (على كثير) ولم يقل على كل من خلقنا، لأن الله - جل وعلا - فضل الملائكة،

ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r5.claim: Exegetical reports cite upright walking and using the hands to bring food to the mouth, unlike animals that walk bent and eat with their mouths.
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r5.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن فضيلة ابن آدم أنه يمشي قائما وأن الدواب والإبل والحمير وما أشبهها تمشي منكبة

ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r6.claim: Those bodily distinctions are only part of the human favor; discernment, wholesome provision, guidance, and countless other blessings add to it.
ZAJJAJ:v3p251#2/r6.anchor:
وهذا الذي في التفسير هو بعض ما فضل به ابن آدم.
وفضله فيما أعطي من التمييز ورزق من الطيبات وبصر من الهدى

ASAD-NOTES:17:70#n83/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:70#n83/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:70#n83/r1.claim: Human dignity rests on conceptual thought, which makes people superior in this respect to other living beings and angels; this continues the theme of verse 61.
ASAD-NOTES:17:70#n83/r1.anchor: by bestowing upon them the faculty of conceptual thinking

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p382#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p382#2/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p382#2/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that angels asked why humans received worldly enjoyment and requested it in the afterlife; God swore He would not equate righteous human offspring with a creature He made by command.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p382#2/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولقد كرمنا بني آدم ﴾ الآية قال قالت الملائكة يا ربنا أعطيت بني آدم الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r1.claim: The passage continues God's favors by mentioning human honor, provision, and distinction after ships and rescue from drowning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى ما امتن به عليهم من إزجاء الفلك في البحر ومن تنجيتهم من الغرق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r2.claim: Alternatively, after threatening sinking and drowning for ingratitude, God lists blessings to prompt gratitude, abandonment of disbelief, and obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r2.anchor: أو لما هددهم بما هدد من الخسف والغرق وأنهم كافرو نعمته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r3.claim: The doubled verb means God made humans possess honor and manifold merits, as when a garment or horse is called noble; it is not wealth-based nobility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r3.anchor: وكرم معدى بالتضعيف من كرم أي جعلناهم ذوي كرم بمعنى الشرف والمحاسن الجمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r4.claim: Exegetical examples of human distinction are illustrative, not exhaustive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r4.anchor: وما جاء عن أهل التفسير من تكريمهم وتفضيلهم بأشياء ذكرها هو على سبيل التمثيل لا على الحصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says human distinction consists in intellect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r5.anchor: كما روي عن ابن عباس أن التفضيل بالعقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says it consists in speech.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r7.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r7.claim: Ata says it consists in balanced, upright stature.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says it consists in foods and pleasures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r8.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم بالمطاعم واللذات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r9.speaker: يمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p83/r9.claim: Yaman says it consists in beauty of form.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says human distinction includes God making Muhammad one of humankind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r1.anchor: محمد بن كعب بجعل محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام منهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir says human distinction consists in making humans rule over and subdue other creatures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r2.anchor: وعن ابن جرير بالتسليط على غيره من الخلق وتسخيره له.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r3.claim: One view identifies the distinction as writing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r4.claim: Another view points to the man's beard and the woman's forelock.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says humans eat with their hands, unlike other creatures that eat with their mouths.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: بأكله بيده وغيره بفمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r6.claim: Other explanations are the ability to manage livelihood and afterlife, or God's creation of Adam with His own hand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r6.anchor: وقيل: بتدبير المعاش والمعاد. وقيل: بخلق الله آدم بيده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya notes animals surpass humans in traits such as horse speed and senses, elephant strength, lion courage, and rooster generosity; human distinction is intellect, enabling mastery of animals, knowledge of God, understanding revelation, and bliss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقد ذكر أن من الحيوان ما يفضل بنوع ما ابن آدم كجري الفرس وسمعه وإبصاره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r8.claim: Carrying humans on land and sea is itself a form of their distinction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r8.anchor: وحملناهم في البر والبحر وهذا أيضا من تكريمهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says humans travel on land by horses, mules, donkeys, and camels, and on sea by ships.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: في البر على الخيل والبغال والحمير والإبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r10.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r10.claim: Another interpreter paraphrases land and sea transport as riding on living flesh and dry wood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r10.anchor: وقال غيره: على أكباد رطبة وأعواد يابسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r11.claim: The “good things” may mean lawful provisions or pleasant things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r11.anchor: والطيبات كما تقدم الحلال أو المستلذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r12.claim: Animals receive provisions less extensively because they do not earn money or wear clothes and generally eat unprepared food, unlike humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r12.anchor: ولا يتسع غيره من الحيوان في الرزق اتساعه لأنه يكتسب المال ويلبس الثياب ويأكل المركب من الأطعمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r13.speaker: طائفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r13.claim: One group takes “many” literally and says humans outrank all creatures except Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, Azrail, and their peers; this is attributed to Ibn Abbas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r13.anchor: فقالت طائفة: فضلوا على الخلائق كلهم غير جبريل وميكائيل وإسرافيل وعزرائيل وأشباههم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r14.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says humans are not superior to angels; al-Zajjaj chooses this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r14.anchor: وعنه إن الإنسان ليس أفضل من الملك وهو اختيار الزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r15.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r15.claim: Ibn Atiyya says animals and jinn are among the less-favored many, while angels are outside that group.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والحيوان والجن هو الكثير المفضول والملائكة هم الخارجون عن الكثير المفضول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r16.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r16.claim: Another group argues the verse proves angels superior because they are exempted from “many,” citing 4:172; Abu Hayyan says this is not entailed and the verse does not compare humans and jinn with angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r16.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الآية تقضي بفضل الملائكة على الإنس من حيث هم المستثنون، وقد قال تعالى لا الملائكة المقربون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says “many of what We created” excludes angels and mocks those who claim humans outrank angels, whose station before God is high.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r17.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: على كثير ممن خلقنا هو ما سوى الملائكة عليهم الصلاة والسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r18.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r18.claim: Other interpretations say humans are preferred through conquest or through their reward in the afterlife; neither addresses the disputed ranking of humans and angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p85/r18.anchor: وقيل: وفضلناهم على كثير بالغلبة والاستيلاء. وقيل: بالثواب والجزاء يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r1.claim: The suggestion that kathīr figuratively means all is unsuitable here: saying humanity was preferred over all creation would be inelegant and unlike Qur’anic eloquence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r1.anchor: وقيل: المراد بكثير مجازه وهو إطلاقه على الجميع، والعرب تفعل ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s discussion of human honor borrows from people called philosophers and follows a mode foreign to Arabic expression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r2.anchor: ولأبي عبد الله الرازي كلام في تكريم ابن آدم وتفضيله مستمد من كلام الذين يسمونهم حكماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r3.claim: After listing humanity’s honors in worldly life, God turns to conditions in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p86/r3.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى أنواعا من كرامات الإنسان في الدنيا ذكر شيئا من أحوال الآخرة فقال:

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r1.claim: The Ashʿarite companions, following al-Ashʿarī, deny that the Qurʾān uses sajʿ (rhymed prose).
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r1.anchor: ذهب أصحابنا كلهم إلى نفي السجع من القرآن وذكره الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعري رضي الله عنه

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r2.speaker: كثير ممن يخالفهم
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r2.claim: Many opponents affirm sajʿ in the Qurʾān and regard it as a source of eloquence, like paronomasia and iltifāt.
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r2.anchor: وذهب كثير ممن يخالفهم إلى إثبات السجع في القرآن وزعموا أن ذلك مما يبين به فضل الكلام

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r3.speaker: كثير ممن يخالفهم
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r3.claim: Their evidence is that verse-final rhyme accounts for reversing the order of Moses and Aaron in two passages, although Moses is considered superior.

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r4.speaker: كثير ممن يخالفهم
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r4.claim: They distinguish rhyme from poetry: accidental metrical speech is not poetry, whereas Qurʾānic sajʿ is too frequent to be accidental.
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r4.anchor: وأما ما في القرآن من السجع فهو كثير لا يصح أن يتفق كله غير مقصود إليه

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r5.speaker: أهل اللغة
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r5.claim: The lexicographers define sajʿ as successive speech on a single measure.
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r5.anchor: قال أهل اللغة هو موالاة الكلام على وزن واحد

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r6.speaker: ابن دريد
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r6.claim: Ibn Durayd explains sajʿ of a dove as repeating its voice and cites poetry using the term al-sawājiʿ.
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r6.anchor: وقال ابن دريدسجعت الحمامة معناه رددت صوتها

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r7.claim: Bāqillānī rejects the claim: if the Qurʾān used a familiar Arab form such as sajʿ, that alone could not establish its inimitability; calling it miraculous sajʿ would invite the same claim for poetry.
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r7.anchor: وهذا الذي يزعمونه غير صحيح ولو كان القرآن سجعا لكان غير خارج عن أساليب كلامهم

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r8.claim: Sajʿ’s association with Arab soothsayers makes its absence from the Qurʾān an even stronger proof than the absence of poetry, since soothsaying conflicts with prophecy.
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r8.anchor: وكيف والسجع مما كان يألفه الكهان من العرب ونفيه من القرآن أجدر بأن يكون حجة من نفي الشعر

BAQILLANI:v1p57/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r9.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r9.claim: In a report about compensation for a fetus, the Prophet rebukes a rhymed formulation as resembling the sajʿ of the pre-Islamic age or soothsayers, treating it as blameworthy.
BAQILLANI:v1p57/r9.anchor: فقال أسجاعه كسجاعة الجاهلية وفي بعضها أسجعا كسجع الكهان فرأى ذلك مذموما

BURHAN:v4p302/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r13.claim: Some read في as عن in “blind in the afterlife”: those who disbelieved the worldly blessings described after “We have honored Adam's children” will be blind to afterlife bliss.
BURHAN:v4p302/r13.anchor: أي عن النعيم الذي قلناه ووصفناه في الدنيا فهو في نعيم الآخرة أعمى إذ لم يصدق

ITQAN:v4p519#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r2.claim: A report from Jabir has the Prophet explain human honor as eating with one's fingers.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r1.claim: With innamā, exclusivity falls on whichever of subject or object is delayed: ‘ʿAmr struck Zayd’ singles out the striker, while ‘ʿAmr struck Zayd’ with the object delayed singles out the one struck.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r1.anchor: فكذلك يقع مع ' إنما ' في المؤخر منهما دون المقدم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r2.claim: In al-Farazdaq's line, the intended exclusivity is that he alone, or someone like him, defends the clan's honor, not that he defends only their honor.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r2.anchor: ذاك لأن غرضه أن يخص المدافع لا المدافع عنه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r3.claim: The detached pronoun is necessary to place the delayed subject after the object and secure the intended focus; it is neither grammatical redundancy nor metrical necessity.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p260/r3.anchor: وجملة الأمر أن الواجب أن يكون اللفظ على وجه يجعل الاختصاص فيه للفرزدق

DAMGHANI:v1p302/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r8.claim: Human beings' good provisions include grains, honey, ghee, and other choice foods, which are better than the provisions of animals and birds.
DAMGHANI:v1p302/r8.anchor: ورزقناهم من الطيبات يعني جميع رزق بني ادم الحب والعسل والسمن ونحوه من اطيب الطعام وجعل رزقهم اطيب من رزق الدواب والطير

DAMGHANI:v1p403/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r3.claim: Karīm can mean virtuous or one who bestows favor; the source links God’s honoring humanity with His favor to Adam over Satan.
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r3.anchor: الكريم الفاضل قوله تعالى في سورة الفجر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says karīm means noble or excellent, and can also mean forgiving or beautiful; all senses rest on honor.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الكريم : الشريف الفاضل . ويقال الكريم ويراد به : الصفوح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.claim: The first Quranic sense is excellence or superiority, including God’s honoring Adam’s children and the noble book, messenger, and person.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الكريم في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.claim: Karīm can mean noble, honored, or excellent: the most God-fearing are best, humanity is honored, and the other examples describe rank or honor.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.anchor: الكريم: الشريف الفاضل، قال الله تعالى: إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم [الحجرات: 13]

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r1.claim: An earlier position calls verse endings heads of verses rather than fawāṣil and avoids calling them sajʿ, while still saying Qur'anic composition deliberately attends to sound and matching endings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r1.anchor: لم يذكرها باسم الفواصل وإنما هي عنده رءوس آيات. وقد تحاشى القول "بالسجع" فيها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r2.claim: Until the third Islamic century, scholars avoided the term sajʿ for the Qur'an because it was associated with soothsayers.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r2.anchor: وحتى القرن الثالث للهجرة، كان التحرج واضحاً من القول بالسجع في القرآن، وكأنما كان الحس المؤمن ينبو عن هذه الكلمة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r3.speaker: الأشاعرة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r3.claim: The Ash'arites deny sajʿ in the Qur'an and call its verse endings fawāṣil.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r3.anchor: قرر "الأشاعرة" نفي السجع عن القرآن، وقالوا إنما هي فواصل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r4.speaker: مخالفو الأشاعرة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r4.claim: Many who opposed the Ash'arites accepted Quranic sajʿ as intentional and as a feature that contributes to eloquence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r4.anchor: وذهب كثير ممن يخالفهم إلى إثبات السجع في القرآن. وزعموا أن ذلك مما يبين به فضل الكلام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r5.speaker: الباقلاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r5.claim: Al-Baqillani rejects the opposing claim: if the Qur'an were sajʿ, it would remain within familiar Arab speech and could not establish inimitability; sajʿ also evokes soothsaying.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p254/r5.anchor: ولو كان القرآن سجعا لكان غير خارج عن أساليب كلامهم ولو كان داخلا فيها لم يقع بذلك إعجاز

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p893/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p893/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p893/r1.claim: Mentioning carriage on land and sea encompasses every human from Adam to the end of time; saying only in the air would exclude many, and the surrounding passage also concerns land and sea.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p893/r1.anchor: لو قال (في الجو) لشمل التكريم من حُملوا في الجو وبذلك تكون الآية أغفلت كثيراً من بني آدم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.claim: A righteous, God-fearing, faithful human is more honored by God than the angels; God honored humanity through knowledge and intellect.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.anchor: الإنسان الصالح التقي المؤمن أكرم عند الله تعالى من الملائكة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p892/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p892/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p892/r3.claim: The verse uses past forms for honoring and carrying humans; at revelation's time there was no air transport, so it names carrying by land and sea.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p892/r3.anchor: استعمل صيغة الماضي في الآية (كرّمنا، حملناهم) وفي وقتها لم يكن هناك حملٌ في الجوّ

NASHR:v2p197/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p197/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p197/r1.claim: Recitation study had no fixed maximum duration: one complete reading of Abū Jaʿfar was taken over four months, one daily portion, and other teachers imposed no limit.
NASHR:v2p197/r1.anchor: قرأ بها على أبي عبد الله صالح بن سعيد الرازي ختمة كاملة في مدة أربعة أشهر كل يوم جزء

NASHR:v2p197/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p197/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p197/r4.claim: Examples include Yaʿqūb learning over eighteen months, a full Abū ʿAmr reading being heard in a day, and Ibn Muʾmin reading all readings in seventeen days; Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī completions took four and seven days.
NASHR:v2p197/r4.anchor: قرأ شيخنا أحمد بن الطحان على الشيخ أبي العباس بن نحلة ختمة كاملة بحرف أبي عمرو من روايته في يوم واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r1.claim: Reading from a mushaf helps prevent neglect and lets readers recall omissions, detect altered or misplaced words and verses, and verify recitation; for learning exact performance, oral instruction is better because writing alone often leads to errors.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r1.anchor: فهذه الآثار تدل على أن هذا أمر مطلوب لئلا يعطل المصحف فلا يقرأ منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r2.claim: If reading from writing causes mispronunciation while a qualified teacher is available, Ibn Kathir says to avoid it; when no teacher can be found, necessity permits reading from the mushaf and one is not charged beyond capacity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r2.anchor: فأما عند العجز عمن يلقن فلا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها، فيجوز عند الضرورة ما لا يجوز عند الرفاهية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r3.claim: A traveler reportedly traced to the Prophet the statement that when a servant mispronounces or errs while reading, an angel records it as it was revealed; the narrator is uncertain that it is prophetic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r3.anchor: أن رجلا صحبهم في سفر قال: فحدثنا حديثا ما أعلمه إلا رفعه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r4.speaker: بكير بن الأخنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r4.claim: Bakir b. al-Akhnas relates the saying that when a non-Arab or someone unable to recite correctly reads, the angel records it as revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r4.anchor: عن بكير (2) بن الأخنس قال: كان يقال: إذا قرأ الأعجمي والذي لا يقيم القرآن كتبه الملك كما أنزل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r5.claim: Some scholars make the better mode depend on concentration: recite from memory if more attentive, or from a mushaf if that produces greater concentration; if equal, looking at the mushaf is preferable for accuracy and the added act of looking. Al-Nawawi says this best explains the early authorities' practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r5.anchor: المدار في هذه المسألة على الخشوع في القراءة، فإن كان الخشوع عند القراءة على ظهر القلب فهو أفضل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r6.claim: If al-Bukhari meant Sahl's marriage report to prove reciting from memory is always superior, Ibn Kathir objects: it may have been a special case involving an illiterate man and cannot establish a general rule.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p69/r6.anchor: للدلالة على أن تلاوة القرآن عن ظهر قلب أفضل منها في المصحف، ففيه نظر
